title: Ring rule stays; a protocol exists only where two production adapters exist (retires P-01/P-08 'every adapter behind a port, only the container wires it')
context: P-01 (features-no-infrastructure) and P-08 (cli-no-infrastructure) required every I/O boundary to sit behind a core/protocols Protocol wired only by container.py. Measured reality (0.5.1 deepening audit, re-verified by inspection): core/protocols holds 23 Protocol classes in 22 files, 935 LOC of interface text; only 4 have two or more production adapters — TelemetryRefreshLock, FilePermissionSetter, ShutdownHandler (posix/windows pairs) and ProcessAncestry (Linux proc / ps / Windows toolhelp) — all OS-portability seams; the other 19 have exactly one infrastructure implementer and exist only to satisfy the two contracts. container.py is 880 LOC, 22 fix commits, 10 ledger records carrying 'container.py' as component, ~180 LOC of dead lifecycle closures (_definition_committer, _closure_committer, _memory_lint_gate, _repo_hygiene_sweeper, _workspace_python_bin, resolve_context) kept alive by the funnel. Ledger evidence: a grep of every 'cause'/'solution' field in specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl finds ONE mention of 'adapter' (git shallow-repo guard, fixed inside GitSubprocessClient — not a swap) and ZERO mentions of 'fake'; no bug was ever fixed by substituting an adapter behind a seam. The contracts produced the funnel they were meant to prevent: every verb needing infrastructure added a build_* function to container.py instead of a port, and 9 of the 18 capped ignore edges are exceptions to these two contracts alone (features-no-infrastructure 7, cli-no-infrastructure 2). Test fakes are not a second adapter: git_subprocess has 14 real-adapter test files and 0 fakes.
decision: We will keep the ring rule — core imports nothing internal; infrastructure imports only core; features import core and infrastructure; cli and hooks import all of them; no upward edge; features never import a sibling feature; core.kernel_tunables stays a leaf; core.specs_resolver keeps its single home — and drop the port requirement: a feature or a CLI verb imports the concrete infrastructure class it is the only consumer of, directly. A Protocol lives in core/protocols only where two or more PRODUCTION adapters exist (today: TelemetryRefreshLock, FilePermissionSetter, ShutdownHandler, ProcessAncestry); a test fake never counts as a second adapter. container.py wires only what two features share or what a platform seam selects; everything else is constructed where it is consumed. Replacement Part-1 text — P-01: 'We keep the dependency ring: core imports nothing internal, infrastructure imports only core, no layer imports upward; a feature imports the concrete infrastructure class it alone consumes.' Measured by: `lint-imports --config setup.cfg --no-cache` — contracts core-no-upper-layers and infrastructure-no-upper-layers (zero ignored imports). P-08: 'We keep a Protocol in core/protocols only where two production adapters exist; container.py composes platform seams and shared collaborators, nothing single-consumer.' Measured by: `pytest tests/contract/test_protocols_have_two_adapters.py` (AST walk: every class under core/protocols has >= 2 implementers under infrastructure/), landing in the same commit that retires the 19 single-adapter protocols.
consequences: + setup.cfg: contracts features-no-infrastructure and cli-no-infrastructure are DELETED with their 9 ignore edges; _RECORDED_IGNORE_EDGE_CAP drops 18 -> 9 and _RECORDED_CONTRACT_COUNT 9 -> 7 in the accept commit (P-10 ratchet holds: the cap only falls). The cross-feature edges (6) stay until K7; the features-no-subprocess edges (3) stay under P-02, which is untouched (one process seam, not a swap seam). + ~17 protocol files, their build_* indirections and the two-protocols-per-store pairs are deleted (~935 -> ~200 LOC of protocol text); container.py shrinks to wiring only (~250 LOC); the ~180 LOC dead closures go with it. + Tests use real adapters over tmp dirs, as git_subprocess already does; mirrored fake-based unit files are deleted per dd-test-stewardship. - A feature reaching an adapter directly cannot be substituted without editing the feature; accepted because the ledger shows zero substitutions in the project's history and four real seams remain protected. - P-01/P-08 text in ARCHITECTURE.md changes in the accept commit (`docs(adr): accept ...`), never before. Bug surface: REDUCED — the 880-LOC funnel with 22 fix commits and 10 ledger records is the only component this decision touches, and it shrinks; no ledger bug depends on the retired seams. Dependency: K9's deletion half (dead closures, single-consumer modules filed inside their feature where no contract breaks) proceeds before acceptance; protocol retirement and contract deletion wait for the operator's accept.
measured_by: lint-imports --config setup.cfg --no-cache — contracts core-no-upper-layers, infrastructure-no-upper-layers, features-no-cross-feature, kernel-tunables-is-a-leaf, bind-resolution-seam-is-a-single-home; plus pytest tests/contract/test_import_linter_ignore_cap.py re-pinned at _RECORDED_IGNORE_EDGE_CAP = 9, _RECORDED_CONTRACT_COUNT = 7

title: Git index boundary: one session per checkout is operator practice, not library code; the two shared-index bugs are deferred with that reason
context: Two open records — concurrent-sessions-share-git-index-commit-boundary-contamination (2026-08-27, `git commit --amend` swept a peer's staged histo file) and concurrent-agent-git-add-clobbers-other-sessions-staged-files-into-unrelated-commit (2026-08-27, `git add -A` swept a peer's two staged files) — have one cause: two harness sessions ran Bash in the SAME checked-out repos/<slug> tree, and git keeps exactly one index per worktree. Three options were weighed. (a) `context bind` provisions a per-session linked worktree: bind writes one session record and acquires nothing (context-management memory); a harness process cannot change its cwd after launch, so a worktree created by bind is never the tree the session commits from; gitflow allows exactly one live feature/{M.m.p} and git refuses the same branch checked out in two worktrees, so every extra worktree needs its own branch or a detached HEAD — a second branch pattern the §4 contract forbids; the open bug sdd-gate-memory-phase-resolves-empty-when-cwd-is-a-linked-worktree-outside-repos shows worktrees already break resolution (K1 fixes it); Windows adds per-worktree venv cost. Rejected. (b) pre-commit refuses when the index holds paths staged by a foreign presence: PresenceRecord carries session_id, runtime, pid, last_seen_at — no paths — so the gate would have to start recording every written path per session (new state, new reaper), git cannot attribute who ran `git add`, and the refusal blocks a human commit, violating DADAIA §3.4 (pre-commit warns and always allows) and the NO-LOCKS doctrine. A branch added to pre_commit_decision plus a new record kind is the puxadinho the standing order forbids. Rejected. (c) Nothing in the library: the index is a per-worktree resource by git's own contract; DADAIA §7.3 already states 'commit exactly what the fix touched, never a blanket -A'; the only missing statement is the operator practice.
decision: We will not add library code for the git index. The practice is: one harness session per checked-out tree; an operator who wants parallel sessions on one repo creates the linked worktree BEFORE launching the harness (`git worktree add ../<repo_slug>-<n> <branch>`) and launches it there, so each session owns its own index; every agent stages by explicit path and commits with `git commit --only <paths>` or after a path-scoped `git add`, never `-A` and never a bare `--amend` (DADAIA §7.3 already). The two records move to terminal `deferred` with reason: 'shared git index between two sessions in one checkout is a git contract, not a library contract; practice = one session per checkout/worktree; revisit only if a harness gains a per-session cwd'. Code change: 0 production LOC; owner: none — the practice belongs to the operator and to the law text (a one-line statement under DADAIA.md §3.3 'Races, mode, context', authored by ai-engineer in public/data/DADAIA.md if the operator wants it written).
consequences: + Zero new state, zero new branch, zero new reaper; pre_commit_decision stays WARN-only; presence stays path-less and advisory; bind keeps acquiring nothing; Invocation keeps one session_id. + The K1 fix for the linked-worktree resolution bug makes the practice actually work end to end (a worktree outside repos/ resolves its context). - The defect can still recur whenever an operator launches two harnesses in one tree; the pre-commit advisory WARN ('another session is live on this context') is the only signal, and it already exists. Bug surface: UNCHANGED for the library (no touched feature), and the two records leave the open set with a reason instead of a patch — the 06-10..07-22 session-model chain shows every structural fix in this area was a deletion, never an added guard.
measured_by: python3 .agents/skills/dd-bug-resolution/scripts/bugs.py status --specs repos/dadaia-workspace/specs — both records terminal `deferred` naming this decision; pytest tests/contract/test_hooks_publication_boundary.py (pre-commit remains allow-always)

title: Slop is defined once by the deletion test, distributed over two classes and measured by downward-only ratchets
context: 'slop' was law on 14 surfaces and defined on none, with four implicit meanings and the same rule in up to five homes; no rule covered comments, docstrings, acronyms or SPEC size; constitution §12 (since v0.1.46) did not hold while ratchets V26-V30 did (report 2026-09-03T023255Z-slop-governance-map; operator ruling 2026-09-03 on two distribution classes): rewritten 2026-09-12 (audit ADR-2: named P-29 and an amended P-24 that never existed); accepted by operator decision 2026-09-12
decision: We define slop ONCE, by the deletion test, in DADAIA.md §7.6, and distribute it over two classes: the agentic-class statements stay in §7.6, and the artifact-class statements live as fixed sections projected by the scaffold into constitution.md (slop-law), memory/ARCHITECTURE.md (slop-code) and memory/QUALITY.md (slop-tests), kept byte-exact by the doctor's FIXED-1/FIXED-2 rules; constitution §12 points at §7.6 instead of restating it. The balance is measured by downward-only ratchets: V31 (test files without an `Intent:` header, per tier) in tests/contract/test_test_suite_ratchets.py, and V32 (governance ids in production comments and docstrings), V33 (PREFIX-NN families without a mechanical reader) and V34 (live candidate SPEC.md/TASKS.md bytes) in tests/contract/test_slop_ratchets.py. Detection signals live in dd-code-review/SLOP.md, read by review and by audit pillar 2.
consequences:
+ one definition, one home per statement: a reader greps `deletion test` and finds §7.6, and every artifact restatement is a healed projection rather than a hand-kept copy
+ the balance is a number that only moves down, so 'we cleaned slop' is falsifiable
- four ratchet ceilings must be lowered by hand at each closure, or they rot upward-permissive
measured_by: pytest tests/contract/test_slop_ratchets.py tests/contract/test_test_suite_ratchets.py

title: P-16 deleted: no derived provenance is stored, so nothing needs to equal a re-derivation
context: operator grill ruling 2026-09-12 (SDD lifecycle audit; release 0.4.7 candidate 3 SPEC FR1) — the operator directive of 2026-09-12 (implement and close every registered item) makes the ruling's records accepted at append. P-16 ('a stored resolved_commit equals the value derived from git history') measured a seven-key git-derived cache on the bug record (lineage_source, registration_commit, registration_granularity, resolved_commit, resolution_granularity, root_cause, migration_note) written by core/bug_provenance.py from a full-history walk every CI job fetched (fetch-depth: 0 x13); its only reader was audit pillar 1, which reads git log for the same fact and wrote the cache back; 476 live and 65 archived records carried keys nothing consumed.
decision: Delete P-16 together with the field it measured. The bug record stores no fact a resolver can re-derive from git: core/bug_provenance.py, core/models/git_history.py, GitSubprocessClient.log_added_lines, BugEventKind, BugService.resolved_commit and the seven schema keys are deleted; BugRecord.from_dict ignores exactly the seven retired keys and to_dict never emits them; dadaia doctor --fix (LEDGER-BUGS-SCHEMA) re-serializes every committed record that still carries one; CI checks out at default depth except security-verdict-gate. Lineage stays a declared fact — caused_by, written once at bugs resolve and validated against the ledger or the literal none — because it is a judgement, not a derivation.
consequences:
+ one record shape, one lineage writer, no cache to keep honest and no principle guarding it
+ every CI job but one is a shallow checkout
+ git is the only authority for git facts; pillar 1 reads git log directly
- a consumer tree with pre-0.4.7 records is invalid until dadaia doctor --fix runs once (the fix line is printed under every finding)
- the retired-key tuple in from_dict is a migration and is deletable once every consumer tree has run the fix

title: Every human- and agent-facing document derives from a named memory atom under a content hash
context: operator demand 2026-09-12: the tool must be usable by humans and by agents, and the docs are bad and stale. README.md (15 KB, hand-written beside memory, PyPI's long description) carried eleven verified dead claims (ACTIVE.md/CLOSURE.md, four harnesses, a TTL lease with a PID veto, six-axis reviews, handoffs under specs/releases, event-sourced bugs, dadaia academy and dadaia clean, Academy/Games tabs, memory writable only in two phases, a pre-commit lease gate) and a hand-kept CLI table with two dead verbs; nothing measured a README sentence against the atom that should have produced it, and two of three discovery surfaces (PyPI metadata, the GitHub repository) said nothing. Release 0.4.7 candidate 4 (SPEC FR3/FR4/FR5, Q8) admits the rule as QUALITY.md P-29 with this record proposed; the operator flips it.
decision: We derive every human- and agent-facing document from a named memory atom under a content hash: README.md, llms.txt and every docs/*.md carry under each `## ` heading one or more `<!-- derived-from: <slug> sha256:<12 hex> -->` markers whose slug resolves by stem to exactly one file under specs/memory/ and whose hash is that file's current sha256 prefix; docs/cli.md carries no marker and is the committed output of `dadaia help tree`; there is no generator verb — a stale section is re-derived by a reader and its hash re-recorded in the same commit as the atom (dd-release-implementation MEMORY-UPDATE); the tagline is one sentence across README.md, pyproject.toml `description` and llms.txt; a section that can name no atom is slop, or names a fact memory lacks and the fact enters memory first.
consequences:
+ a doc cannot rot silently: one changed atom byte reddens every section derived from it, and the failure names the atom to re-read and the line to re-record
+ no fact enters a doc that memory does not carry, so memory stays the one product truth and the docs are its projections
+ one finder (features/specs/citations.py::dead_citations) keeps docs, public assets and memory free of dead verbs and paths
- the hash is whole-file: an atom edit touching no derived fact still costs a re-read of every section citing it
- the derived set is a glob: a new docs/*.md is governed at birth and cannot opt out
measured_by: pytest tests/contract/test_docs_derived_from_memory.py

title: Pre-push gate scopes every scan to the pushed range and to the tree's own pattern
context: Operator ruling 2026-09-13 (grill on the [REDACTED-TERM] restart): the pre-push canon scan listed the whole tree at the tip and applied the v6 canon to pattern-5 trees, locking every push of sample-consumer and the legacy explorer; the foreign-slug layer refused new docs naming a sibling repository the repository already published. Bugs pre-push-canon-scan-not-range-scoped and pre-push-foreign-slug-flags-already-published-sibling-name.
decision: The specs canon scan checks only the specs/ paths the pushed range introduces or rewrites, read from the same single object pass as the denylist scan; the verdict rule alone keeps a tree view. The v6 canon predicate does not apply to a specs/ tree stamped below CANONICAL_SPECS_VERSION (one stderr note names `dadaia specs upgrade`). A foreign repo slug already published in the remote tip (or the integration tip for a new ref) is not a new disclosure. Every read failure fails closed.
consequences: Published history never blocks a push; a pre-migration tree pushes until it is migrated, with the doctor reporting the drift; a hook chokepoint never locks the operator's own work. Amends the 2026-08-28 specs-canon closure ruling (whole-tree scan).

title: The release archive holds published versions only; a candidate closed between publications is rc-N of the version that published it
context: Operator ruling 2026-09-14: specs/releases/_archive/ carried 0.5.0, 0.5.1, 0.5.2 and 0.5.3 as archived releases while the live release was 0.4.7 and PyPI's latest was 0.4.6 — versions minted before the release-candidates model (ADR 0005) and never published under those ids; 0.5.2/0.5.3 carried no shipped sha at all. All four (plus the pre-canon v0.4.5) were published together as PyPI 0.4.5 on 2026-08-31 (PR #240). The doctor accepted the shape; the law never stated what the archive may hold.
decision: releases/_archive/<M.m.p>/ holds PUBLISHED versions only. Every candidate closed between two publications is an rc-N/ of the version that published it (the final one at the root, ADR 0009), never its own archived release. dadaia release fold <id> --into <published> [--shipped --pr --shipped-ts] [--final] is the ONE governed repair: trio(s) moved, logs merged in ts order plus one note, the folded directory deleted, the histo record(s) rewritten in place, one governance event. RELEASE-TREE-ARCHIVE-ID (an archived id at or above the live release) and RELEASE-TREE-ARCHIVE-UNSHIPPED (an archived release without shipped sha/pr) are doctor errors naming that verb. Applied at once: 0.4.5 = rc-1 v0.4.5, rc-2 0.5.0, rc-3 0.5.1, rc-4 0.5.2, root 0.5.3.
consequences: The archive reads as the PyPI history: one directory per published version, its candidates inside. A future 'archive without a publication' cannot pass the doctor. The histo keeps every record (ids unchanged, release field = the published version). Hand moves under _archive/ are never the path.
measured_by: pytest tests/contract/test_release_tree_canon.py tests/unit/features/specs/test_candidate_fold.py

title: The workspace holds repos inside it, never a monorepo; one workspace with one repo is the minimal case, and bootstrap is one command
context: Operator ruling 2026-09-18, after the competitive report (22 tools, 8 harnesses): every peer is per-repo (.specify/, .conductor/, .kiro/, .cursor/), per-user or per-org; the level 'my projects' exists only here. The multi-repo workspace with its law, harness projections, .dadaia/ zones, venv and .env OUTSIDE every repo is the principal foundation of the product and must not be diluted into a per-repo or monorepo tool. Adoption evidence: 7 stages before first value vs one-line installs for every tool above 20k stars.
decision: Repos live inside the workspace under repos/<slug>/, each its own git repository with its own specs/; the workspace is never a monorepo and never a nested .dadaia/. A workspace with one repo is the degenerate case of multi-repo, not a separate mode: no context verb is required before the second repo. Bootstrap is one command: the operator runs one uv/uvx line, passes a REQUIRED valid directory name, and receives the complete workspace state; the first repo is OPTIONAL (--repo <url> clones it, births its context ALIVE and binds the shell in the same step); with no URL the operator is oriented to repos/ as the place of work.
consequences: init grows one required argument and one optional --repo; context create/alive/bind disappear from the first-run path; docs and positioning lead with 'your product repos never carry agent config'. Backlog entries one-line-bootstrap, english-only-surface, standalone-skills-distribution, public-presence-and-launch and panel-scope-to-unique-value implement the ruling.
measured_by: pytest tests/e2e/test_one_line_bootstrap.py tests/unit/core/test_workspace_resolver.py

ruling.words: Jamais seremos monorepo. No menor caso somos 1 workspace com 1 repo.

title: Three flows into a release: operator demand, bug composition, backlog; the backlog is optional, a SPEC carries its origin, one candidate is defined at a time and memory updates at every candidate closure
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-20 (dd-grill-me over the 17 backlog entries, rounds 1..3, Q1..Q37). Q24 A a single bug stays Arm B and is fixed immediately; a candidate may be composed of open bugs the operator picks; Q25 A the backlog is optional, SPEC gains origin; Q27 A _ideas dies, rc-N stays, one RC defined at a time, each RC ends with a push and a review by the skill; Q34 A memory updates at each candidate closure; Q8 A the PM writes SPEC and memory, the engineer writes PLAN and TASKS. The 2026-07-15 hotfix doctrine stands: a bug never waits for a release.
decision: Flow 1 (default): operator demand -> SPEC -> PLAN/TASKS -> implementation -> memory -> closure. Flow 2 (bug composition): open bugs picked by the operator -> bug-only candidate; memory surgical or none. Flow 3 (backlog): research-grade items -> candidate with the heaviest memory pass. Every candidate SPEC carries **Origin:** operator-demand | backlog:<slug>[,<slug>] | bugs:<id>[,<id>], required by the doctor. §1.1 changes: a feature enters through the backlog OR through an operator demand recorded as the SPEC origin; a confirmed bug is still fixed at once, and may additionally be composed into a candidate. Exactly one candidate trio exists at the release root; the next is born only after rc-archive. Memory is updated in every candidate's closure, never deferred to promote.
consequences: dd-release-definition loses the mandatory pick-from-backlog step and gains the origin field; specs/releases/_ideas/ leaves the canon; dd-bug-resolution gains the composition note. The PM/engineer split of the trio replaces the product-engineer owner row.

title: context create is the one level-2 verb: clone, hook, ALIVE and bind in one transactional step; the frozen-surface law is amended
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-23 ('sigo recomendações', answering D1-D13 of the onboarding grill) and execution order 2026-09-24; SPEC 0.4.8 candidate 1 'onboarding in three levels' (45620ce5). AS-IS: onboarding needed create -> alive -> bind plus an implicit specs scaffold inside alive; a failed create/alive left a DEAD context owning the slug (R3), alive never installed the pre-push hook (R5), and the create/alive split is the recurring bug site (context.py 8 bugs, spec_context/service.py 7).

The `.dadaia/AGENTS.md` line 'the context surface is frozen' is amended: create's options changed, still no new verb, state file or session field.

title: A foreign specs tree, or a dadaia tree below v6, is renamed to specs-bkp in the main repo before the canon is scaffolded; no migration chain below v6
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-23 ('sigo recomendações', answering D1-D13 of the onboarding grill) and execution order 2026-09-24; SPEC 0.4.8 candidate 1 'onboarding in three levels' (45620ce5). No migration chain is reopened for trees below v6.

title: Re-running init on an existing workspace is the upgrade
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-23 ('sigo recomendações', answering D1-D13 of the onboarding grill) and execution order 2026-09-24; SPEC 0.4.8 candidate 1 'onboarding in three levels' (45620ce5). AS-IS: no documented upgrade path; docs claimed the install works offline.
decision: `uvx dadaia-workspace@X init <ws>` on an existing workspace compares the venv version: newer reinstalls X into the stdlib venv (pip, no uv installer) and runs reconcile, printing 'upgraded A -> B'; equal prints 'already at A' and writes nothing; older exits 1 with the fix naming the installed version. AS-IS: onboarding.next_step derives levels 1-3 but level 3 ends at a stamp (audits_histo) and never reaches commit/push; fix lines are built in several places (FIXED-2/TREE-5 cite a different remedy than the docs, Windows lines are POSIX); SessionStart printed the step only for bound sessions.
decision: features/workspace/onboarding.py owns the ONE ordered list of steps; each step is (real-state predicate, kind command|agent, one fix line built from cli_path by one builder). Invariants: I1 every predicate reads real state (files, git), never a stamp; I2 one portable fix-line builder; I3 executing a step's fix removes that step (property-tested); I4 the loop terminates. doctor, init, context create and SessionStart print the same step; the agent loop is: run doctor, execute the fix of Next:, repeat until no Next:.
consequences: Every onboarding fix line is built once; runtime finding messages that name an onboarding remedy (FIXED-2, TREE-5) delegate to the step builder; an autopilot E2E executes only printed fix lines from an empty directory to a published project.
measured_by: pytest tests/unit/features/workspace/test_onboarding.py tests/e2e/test_onboarding_journey.py

title: Level 3c: context baseline is the one explicit publish verb of an onboarded project
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-24 (onboarding foundation grill, rounds 1-2, Q1-Q11; audit #5 report 2026-09-24 scored 75/100 after the Arm B batch). AS-IS: baseline works only on an unborn repo and pushes feature/0.1.0 with no main or develop; doctor was green with everything uncommitted (C4); ADR 0030 forbids verbs that commit implicitly during onboarding.
decision: `context baseline` is generalised: ensure the principal and integration branches on the remote (unborn repo: both born from one empty root commit; principal present, integration absent: integration born at the principal's tip; present: reused), cut <work>/<version> (0.1.0 with no tag, else last tag + 1 patch) from the integration branch, commit only the paths onboarding wrote (specs/, specs-bkp/, the repo AGENTS.md), push. Level 3c is pending while those paths are untracked or absent from every remote <work>/* branch. The verb runs only when invoked; no other verb commits.
consequences: ADR 0030 is amended: implicit commits stay forbidden, the one explicit publish verb commits. baseline refuses a dirty tree outside the onboarding paths with a fix line.
measured_by: pytest tests/e2e/test_onboarding_journey.py

title: The pre-push gate implements the bootstrap birth of the principal and integration branches with zero new content
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-24 (onboarding foundation grill, rounds 1-2, Q1-Q11; audit #5 report 2026-09-24 scored 75/100 after the Arm B batch). AS-IS: dd-gitflow-default states develop is cut from main at bootstrap only, but pre-push refuses every develop/main push and its fix (gh pr create --base develop) fails while develop does not exist: a consumer's first PR had no target.
decision: A push that creates the principal or integration branch is allowed only when the remote ref does not exist AND the pushed commit publishes no new object (it is already on the remote, or it is the empty root commit). Every other push to those branches stays refused with its fix. No gh dependency: works on GitHub, GitLab and file:// remotes.
consequences: A test proves no new object is published by an allowed birth; the refusal fix lines name the configured branch names.
measured_by: pytest tests/unit/features/chokepoints/test_push_branch_policy.py

title: The project gitflow lives in the constitution frontmatter and the pre-push gate reads it at push time
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-24 (onboarding foundation grill, rounds 1-2, Q1-Q11; audit #5 report 2026-09-24 scored 75/100 after the Arm B batch). The operator asked for a default gitflow users can change per Spec Context Project, shown and confirmed at onboarding, enforced by git hooks. AS-IS: three hard-coded regexes in features/chokepoints/branch_policy.py; git-flow AVH keeps names in the per-clone .git/config (drift between clones), validate-branch-name/lefthook keep a versioned file read by a thin hook.
decision: specs/constitution.md frontmatter carries `gitflow: {principal, integration, work}`; roles are fixed, names are free (principal detected from origin/HEAD, integration default develop, work default feature/{M.m.p}; the version segment is always M.m.p). specs init takes --principal/--integration/--work-prefix and writes the block; the agent shows the detected gitflow to the operator and asks before running it; no confirmation stamp is stored. The pre-push gate reads the block on every push (no copy, so no compare audit); an absent or malformed block falls back to the default with a warning, never a block, and doctor reports GITFLOW-1 with a fix. No pre-commit hook: enforcement sits only at the publication boundary. Root AGENTS.md and dd-gitflow-default direct agents to the project's constitution gitflow.
consequences: The three hard-coded branch regexes are deleted; branch_policy takes the parsed gitflow as input. Trunk-based (no integration branch) is a backlog item.
measured_by: pytest tests/unit/features/chokepoints/test_push_branch_policy.py

title: Every definition reviews the as-is implementation before it adds: DELETE, REBUILD, UPDATE, KEEP, then ADD
context: Operator demand and grill ruling 2026-09-25 (Q1-Q5 accepted): 'jamais declarar uma nova release onde só se empilha novas coisas' — agents defined SPECs that built new behaviour on top of units that should have been rebuilt (bug history: 9 fix-line bugs patched per call site, 8 hard-coded-branch bugs patched per literal, baseline's convergent branch). dd-release-definition went from picking the set straight to the grill and the SPEC; only one sentence asked PLAN to name what it grows or deletes.
decision: Definition step 2, between picking the set and the grill: dd-software-engineer reviews the as-is code the demand touches (read-only). PLAN section 1 'As-is review' is a Markdown table — unit, what it does today, bugs, verdict (DELETE | REBUILD | UPDATE | KEEP), why — followed by ADD rows only for what no existing unit can carry, each justified. REBUILD is mandatory when the unit carries 2 or more bugs, the demand changes its fundamental behaviour, the change would need a flag/branch/special case/second path, or its contract contradicts the demand. SPEC gains 'Replaces' (current behaviours that stop existing). TASKS order DELETE/REBUILD (expand-contract) before ADD. Mechanical: `release.py phase IMPLEMENTATION` refuses a PLAN without the table or with a row whose verdict is outside the vocabulary (structure only, one fix line); dd-code-review's spec axis flags a DELETE/REBUILD unit left unchanged (HIGH) and a KEEP unit that grew. Arm B: when dd-bug-resolution Phase 0 finds 2 or more prior fixes on the same unit, the fix is a REBUILD of that unit, stated in the commit body and --solution.
consequences: Trigger judgement stays with the engineer and the reviewer; no bug counting or code analysis is automated. The root map's Arm A flow names the step; the two engineer personas gain one line each; the release-lifecycle atom is rewritten at closure.
measured_by: pytest tests/contract/test_release_script.py

ruling.words: jamais declarar uma nova release onde só se empilha novas coisas

title: .dadaiaignore is the operator's one file of legitimate workspace paths: operator-only, one meaning, one reader for gate and doctor
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-26 (c5, rounds 1-2, Q1, Q3, Q6); source handoff 2026-09-26T211000Z-main-thread-grill-050-c4-c5-c6 (copy: reports/main-thread/20260927-050-c4-evidence/handoffs/) findings[3],[5],[9]. Today the operator channel is .dadaia/states/instance_exceptions.txt (ADR 0058), which an agent could append to itself via the root BLOCK's printf >> fix line, and the gate and the doctor read root legitimacy by different rules.
decision: We will replace .dadaia/states/instance_exceptions.txt 1:1 with a root .dadaiaignore that declares only operator-legitimate paths (verdict OPERATOR) and means nothing else; the library canon stays in code, never in this file. Only the operator edits it; the gate classes it PROTECTED. A root BLOCK's fix line names .dadaia/tmp/<agent>/<date>/, never the file. It applies to the workspace root, the harness directories and the .dadaia/ top level; never to the tmp TTL nor to repo interiors. The gate and the doctor read it through one function.
consequences: + Ends agent self-legalization and the gate/doctor systemic ambiguity on root entries. - The Q6 clause 'harness directories' meets ADR 0059 (the doctor judges only ledger-owned harness entries); not resolved here, carried as an open question in backlog dadaiaignore-and-root-core-canon. Delivery: 0.5.0 (ADR 0101).
measured_by: pytest tests/unit/hooks/test_root_whitelist.py tests/unit/hooks/test_pre_gate.py (the delivering candidate adds the .dadaiaignore cases)

title: .dadaiaignore grammar: one root-relative pattern per line, # comments, * within one segment, trailing / for a whole directory; no ! and no **; stdlib parser
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-26 (c5, Q5 + R3: simple, no new dependency); source handoff 2026-09-26T211000Z-main-thread-grill-050-c4-c5-c6 (copy: reports/main-thread/20260927-050-c4-evidence/handoffs/) findings[8]. All 17 instance_exceptions.txt lines of the live instance fit the grammar.
decision: We will read .dadaiaignore as: one pattern per line; lines starting with # are comments; paths are workspace-root-relative; * matches within one path segment; a trailing / covers the whole directory; ! (negation) and ** are not admitted; the parser is standard library only. An invalid line is a doctor finding, never a crash and never silently dropped.
consequences: + No gitignore-library dependency, one small parser. - Negation and recursive globs are unavailable by design.
measured_by: pytest tests/unit/core/test_workspace_layout_zones.py (the delivering candidate adds the grammar cases)

title: Core protection has two layers: the gate blocks agent writes to core law and state files; doctor --fix at every SessionStart self-heals missing core; no Bash parsing
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-26 (c5, R2: Bash parsing is fragile); source handoff 2026-09-26T211000Z-main-thread-grill-050-c4-c5-c6 (copy: reports/main-thread/20260927-050-c4-evidence/handoffs/) findings[7]. R2's fourth clause (a missing .venv is fixed by 'uvx dadaia-workspace init <ws>') meets ADR 0067 (without the venv every gate wrapper warns and exits 0) and the open bug missing-venv-hook-disarms-the-gate-invisibly; that clause is not decided here and is carried as an open question in backlog dadaiaignore-and-root-core-canon.

context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-26 (c6, Q9 + R7); source handoff 2026-09-26T211000Z-main-thread-grill-050-c4-c5-c6 (copy: reports/main-thread/20260927-050-c4-evidence/handoffs/) findings[10]. title: Worktrees serve only release implementation and bug fixes; specs are never edited in one except TASKS.md task markers; merging any other specs/ change is refused
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-26 (c6, R8); source handoff 2026-09-26T211000Z-main-thread-grill-050-c4-c5-c6 (copy: reports/main-thread/20260927-050-c4-evidence/handoffs/) findings[11].

Inside a worktree specs/ is never edited except the task markers of TASKS.md; the merge refuses a worktree branch carrying any other specs/ change. Skills and rules teach this; the merge enforces it.

title: A worktree always ends merged into repos/<repo> and then deleted; verbs audit, recognize and clean it; cleaning is the worst case
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-26 (c6, R8 lifecycle); source handoff 2026-09-26T211000Z-main-thread-grill-050-c4-c5-c6 (copy: reports/main-thread/20260927-050-c4-evidence/handoffs/) findings[10] and findings[16].fix_recommendation. Operator: a lost worktree 'is the terror of anyone'.

A precise workflow makes a lost worktree or unmerged work impossible; workspace verbs audit (list, with orphan wt/* branches reported by list and doctor), recognize and clean worktrees; cleaning is the worst case, never the norm, and never deletes a commit.

title: Bind is context plus write scope: a bound session gets constitution.md and the memory injection, and writes only its context's repos and their canonical worktrees; the file-tool gate refuses an out-of-scope write and an always-on rule forbids one by Bash
context: Operator rulings 2026-09-29 in the main-thread session, first-hand: 'se é feito um bind ... o agente deveria ter gerencia somente sobre repos/ parte daquele spec context project e a constitution.md + partes de memory injetadas ... Pode até ver procurando no disco outros repositórios ... para consulta, mas o bind faz a sessão ficar restrita aos repositórios do spec context project ... com as worktrees que serão derivadas dos repos, essa permissão se estenderá'; and, answering that Bash writes are never judged: 'Devemos proibir write e orientar por rule always-on o trabalho'. Today (feature/0.5.0 HEAD ca16acd7): scope knows only repos/<slug>/ (core/invocation.py:165-177 and a second decider hooks/sdd_gate.py:17-23), a write under worktrees/ is refused by the root whitelist (core/workspace_layout.py:262), ctx-inject injects state and never law so constitution.md is not injected (hooks/ctx_inject.py:74-95; memory context-management 'injects state, never law'), and a Bash write is never judged (root map section 3). The bind history holds 82 ledger records (13 CRITICAL): every family built on per-session state (modes, leases, presence, epochs, liveness) bred the next bug and every fix that closed one was a deletion.
decision: We will define bind as context plus write scope and nothing else. Context: a bound session receives its context's specs/constitution.md and the injected memory parts at bind, SessionStart and compaction. Scope: a bound session writes only under repos/<r>/ and worktrees/<r>/<name>/ for every r among the context's main and associated repos, plus the always-writable ADDITIVE zones outside worktrees; it may read anything on disk. A path under worktrees/<r>/ belongs to repo r exactly as repos/<r>/ does. The file-tool gate refuses an out-of-scope write; an always-on rule in the root law forbids an out-of-scope write by any other path, Bash included, and orients the work; the gate does not parse Bash (ADR 0096 stands). Bind carries no concurrency role: parallel work is isolated by canonical worktrees (ADR 0097), never by modes, leases, holders or liveness.
consequences: + Amends the memory statement 'The ctx-inject hook injects state, never law' (specs/memory/product/platform/context-management.md): constitution.md is now injected. + Answers the first clause of canonical-worktrees round-3 question 4 (gate scope for worktrees/<repo>/<name>/ maps to repo <repo>) and open question (3) of backlog dadaiaignore-and-root-core-canon: the idea gate-judges-bash-writes is rejected, the Bash side is law. - An out-of-scope Bash write is forbidden by law, not refused by code. - The two path-to-repo deciders must become one (systemic ambiguity). Delivery: candidate 6 inside 0.5.0 (ADRs 0101, 0102); the touch-point inventory is scratchpad bindreport/TOUCHPOINTS.md of the 2026-09-29 analysis.
measured_by: pytest tests/unit/features/spec_context/test_gate_policy.py tests/integration/test_one_bind.py tests/e2e/features/test_ctx_inject_bind_boundary.py (the delivering candidate adds: bound to X, a write under worktrees/<Y>/ is refused and under worktrees/<X>/ allowed; constitution.md present in the bound injection)

ruling.words: Devemos proibir write e orientar por rule always-on o trabalho

title: A dated .dadaia/tmp directory expires one day after its own mtime, whatever it holds; the TTL walk judges each zone entry once by its own lstat and never descends into it
context: The rebuild of the TTL lane (ee7caca3, bug reaper-judges-ttl-by-walking-every-file) replaced the newest-content bubbling with a per-entry judgment at layout depth (tmp/<agent>/<YYYYMMDD>, handoff/<ctx>/<file>, reaped/<YYYYMMDD>/<top>): the SessionStart lane went 5.99 s -> 0.20 s on 150k live files and doctor lines 50006 -> 7. That reverses the resolved expected clause of reaper-needs-many-runs-for-a-nested-expired-tree ('judged by its newest content'): a dated dir holding live nested scratch now dies one day after its own mtime. The group-A review (dd-code-reviewer, head 1c9417df) flagged the reversal as unrecorded. Operator ruling 2026-09-29, first-hand: 'Aceitar + gravar ADR'.
decision: We will judge every TTL-zone entry by its own lstat at layout depth and never descend into it: a dated tmp directory expires one day after its own mtime, whatever it holds, and work that outlives the day continues in today's dated directory (tmp-AGENTS.md). A linked git worktree is never moved or deleted by the reaper or the sweep (the guard in sweep.move/remove stands); canonical worktrees live under worktrees/, never under .dadaia/tmp (ADR 0097).
consequences: + The reaper's cost is linear in zone entries, not files; the three-bug chain on this surface (reaper-needs-many-runs, doctor-ttl-walk-quadratic, reaper-judges-ttl-by-walking-every-file) is closed by deletion. + Supersedes the expected clause 'judged by its newest content' of reaper-needs-many-runs-for-a-nested-expired-tree; that record is write-once and stays as history. - Scratch nested in yesterday's dated dir is reaped after its day even if touched today; an agent that needs it longer re-creates it under today's dir.
measured_by: pytest tests/contract/cli/test_doctor_scan_cli.py::test_the_session_lane_costs_one_lstat_per_zone_entry_whatever_it_holds

title: repos/<r> receives only merges: every agent write happens inside a canonical worktree; the file-tool gate refuses an agent write under repos/<r>/ with a fix creating the worktree of the right kind
context: Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). Q1 asked 'Os repos em `repos/<r>` passam a receber só merges?'. Operator: 'Sim'. Today ADR 0098 sends release definition, memory, bug and backlog registration to repos/<r>; the races the round-1 report lists as remaining (specs/, the ledgers, the index of the official checkout) all live there, while the fast-forward merge is already serial by git itself. Recommendation accepted with its cost: 'até uma mudança de uma linha passa por criar a worktree, commitar e mergear'.
decision: We will let repos/<r> receive only merges: every agent write happens inside a canonical worktree worktrees/<r>/<name> and reaches repos/<r> only through the merge ritual (ADR 0109). The file-tool gate refuses an agent file-tool write under repos/<r>/ with 'fix: worktree.py new <r> --kind <kind>' naming the kind whose allowed set holds the path (ADR 0106); the always-on rule of ADR 0103 forbids the same write by Bash. The onboarding verbs (context create/alive, specs init, context baseline) and the operator's hand edits are unaffected.
consequences: + Ends the races on specs/, the ledgers and the official checkout's index; only the fast-forward remains, serialized by git. + Supersedes 0098 (definition, memory and registration in repos/; specs never edited in a worktree): with ADR 0106 every stage has its worktree kind. - Even a one-line change pays create, commit, review and merge. - The append-only areas stop being always-writable under repos/<r>; ADR 0106's 'audits need no worktree' is the one stated exception, and how an audit write lands in repos/<r> is open in grill round 2. - ADR 0072's unbound refusal stands; a bound session's refusal under repos/<r>/ now names a worktree, not a bind.
measured_by: pytest tests/unit/features/spec_context/test_gate_policy.py tests/unit/hooks/test_sdd_gate.py (the delivering candidate adds: a bound agent's file-tool write under repos/<r>/ is refused with fix 'worktree.py new <r> --kind <kind>'; the same write under worktrees/<r>/<name>/ is allowed; an onboarding verb's write is not refused)

title: Four worktree kinds — impl, bug, backlog, release — each with a mechanically checked allowed set; audits need no worktree; parallel worktrees are allowed; the merge is the critical moment and judges the spec as a whole
context:
Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). Q2 proposed five kinds (impl, bug, backlog, release, audit) with an allowed set each, checked mechanically at merge. Operator: 'Isso. algumas considerações:
- O merger verificará por exemplo registros que ficariam stale com aquele novo registro. bastante aplicavel a backlog. Releases também. Verificaria se a worktree violaria o padrão de releases, tentando mergear uma release criada com mesmo numero de uma release ja existente. PAra implementação, Se worktrees em paralelo mudam a implementação. haverá conflitos. Pode ser que 2 worktrees trabalhem em paralelo na implementação de uma release. isso é possivel e aceitavel. mas o merge é um momento critico e deve ser criterioso, observando sempre o que está na spec como um todo.
Outros pontos:
- Ao criar uma worktree para implementar uma release no repo principal de onde foi derivada a worktree as specs ja contem a definição final da release.
- 2 worktrees ou mais podem estar fazendo diferentes partes do processo.
- Entenda o fundamental, uma boa governança aqui habilita o trabalho em paralelo seguro. Devemo seguir por esse caminho, identificando os elos fracos, como `como derivar worktrees` e criterios claros para mergear, para cada etapa (bug, backlog release definition e release implementation).
- Audits não precisam de worktrees.' The bug kind also resolves F5 of the round-1 report: the shape-3 fix commit (code + regression test + the BUGS.jsonl line) could not fit ADR 0098's split.
decision: We will have exactly four worktree kinds, each with an allowed set the merge checks mechanically, refusing any file outside it: impl — code, tests, repo docs and TASKS.md task markers; bug — specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl, plus code and tests for a fix, so the whole shape-3 fix commit fits in one worktree; backlog — specs/backlog/BACKLOG.json and specs/ADRs/decisions.jsonl; release — specs/releases/<M.m.p>/**, specs/ADRs/decisions.jsonl and specs/memory/** (memory at closure). Audits need no worktree. Parallel worktrees are allowed, of different kinds and of the same kind, two impl worktrees on the same release included. An impl worktree is created only when the specs of the repo it derives from already hold the release's final definition. The merge is the critical moment: it judges the change against the spec as a whole — e.g. backlog entries the new record makes stale, a release or candidate number that already exists, sibling impl worktrees that changed the same implementation. The per-kind merge criteria are defined by the merge ritual (ADR 0109) and detailed in a later ADR.
consequences: + Every SDD stage (bug, backlog, release definition, release implementation) has one kind and one allowed set; 'uma boa governança aqui habilita o trabalho em paralelo seguro'. + Supersedes 0098 together with ADR 0105. - The weak links the operator names stay to be closed: how a worktree is derived and the per-kind merge criteria (grill round 2, R2-4/R2-5), and the mechanism proving the final definition exists before an impl worktree is created. - Parallel impl worktrees on one release will conflict; the merge, not the creation, is where that is judged.

title: A worktree is named worktrees/<repo>/<M.m.p><letter>-<kind> on the local branch wt/<same>; the letter is the lowest free one per repo and version; the kind is derived from the path, never stored
context: Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). Q3 proposed the kind as a suffix, e.g. worktrees/dadaia-workspace/0.5.0a-impl and …/0.5.0b-backlog, so the merge picks its ritual and allowed set from the path alone — the ADR 0103 doctrine that what can be derived from the path is derived from the path. Operator: 'Isso. Mas atenção na politica de cleanup. não podemos falhar nela. não quero worktrees acumulando pois criaremos muitas. precisamos de uma forma direta e deterministica de manter esse controle e higiene.'
decision: We will name every workspace worktree worktrees/<repo>/<M.m.p><letter>-<kind>, kind one of impl, bug, backlog, release (ADR 0106), on the local branch wt/<M.m.p><letter>-<kind>, never pushed (ADR 0097 stands). The letter is the lowest free one for that repo and version. The kind is derived from the path and never stored anywhere; list, merge and clean read it from the name. Cleanup is direct and deterministic and must never fail: its policy is ADR 0112.
consequences: + No metadata: path and branch name carry id and kind. + The ADR 0097 id <M.m.p><letter> is unchanged, it only gains the suffix. - A lowest-free letter is reused after a merge, so a letter never identifies a worktree across time; its commits do (ADR 0108). - The deterministic cleanup mechanism the operator requires is open in grill round 2 (R2-7).

title: Git is the worktree registry: no worktree JSON under .dadaia/states/; git worktree list, refs/heads/wt/* and the branch reflog answer every question; a worktree's purpose lives in its commits
context: Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). Q4 asked whether to keep a control JSON under .dadaia/states/. Recommendation: do not create it — a second list next to the one git already keeps is two sources of truth for one question, the pattern that bred the 82 bind bugs, and ADR 0027 forbids a new state file. Operator: 'Então vamos ver o que é melhor. Sigo sua recomendação desde que seja seguro e robusto e tenhamos uma boa governança.' Established by inspection: git worktree list --porcelain gives each worktree's path, HEAD, branch and locked/prunable state; the branch reflog gives its creation date.
decision: We will keep no worktree state file. The registry is git: git worktree list --porcelain, refs/heads/wt/* and the wt/ branch reflog for age. A worktree's purpose (the task, bug or backlog id) lives in its commits. list, doctor, merge and clean derive every answer from these and write no state of their own.
consequences: + Reaffirms ADR 0027: no new state file or session field. + No second list that can diverge. - The operator's condition ('seguro e robusto') is the measure: a question git cannot answer is a new ADR, never a side file.

title: The worktree merge ritual has five steps: clean tree; rebase onto the work branch; the mechanical per-kind check; the dd-code-reviewer judgment; the main thread fast-forwards, removes the worktree and runs branch -d
context: Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). Q5 proposed a numbered list in the gitflow skill: (1) all committed, a dirty worktree refused; (2) rebase onto the work branch, conflicts resolved in the worktree, never in repos/; (3) the mechanical check of the kind — files inside the allowed set, the ledger check passes (bugs.py check, backlog.py check, release.py check), repo tests green for impl and bug; (4) dd-code-reviewer judgment with the kind's checklist; (5) the main thread runs worktree.py merge: fast-forward into repos/<r>, remove the worktree, delete the branch with branch -d, never -D. Recommendation: 'aprovar como está. Quem mergeia é a thread principal, porque o checkpoint de revisão é dela.' Operator: 'Sim, sigo a recomendação.' Inspection: ADR 0018 keeps in the CLI only what touches .dadaia/ and says scripts never call each other, so the ritual is a numbered skill list.
decision: We will merge every worktree by five steps, a numbered list in dd-gitflow-default: 1. the worktree is clean, a dirty one is refused; 2. rebase onto the repo's work branch, conflicts resolved in the worktree, never in repos/; 3. the mechanical per-kind check — the allowed set (ADR 0106), the ledger checks, the repo tests for impl and bug; 4. the dd-code-reviewer judgment with the kind's checklist (ADR 0110); 5. the main thread runs the merge — fast-forward into repos/<r>, remove the worktree, branch -d, never -D. dd-gitflow-default's scripts/worktree.py does the mechanics; there is no CLI verb (ADR 0018), and worktree.py never calls another skill script.
consequences: + A conflict is never resolved in repos/; repos/<r> only fast-forwards. + branch -d refuses an unmerged branch, so the merge cannot delete a commit (ADR 0099). - One reviewer round per merge. - The per-kind criteria behind steps 3 and 4 are detailed in a later ADR (grill round 2, R2-5); the Q5 checklists (backlog redundancy, staleness, ADR contradiction, operator provenance; bug duplicate, bug-or-feature, caused_by; release SPEC coherence with backlog and ADRs; impl three axes and markers matching commits) are the seed.
measured_by: the delivering candidate adds: pytest tests/integration/test_worktree_lifecycle.py (merge refuses a dirty worktree and a non-fast-forward; a failed fast-forward removes nothing; a successful merge fast-forwards repos/<r>, removes the worktree and deletes wt/<name> with -d)

title: Review is machine-required for a worktree merge: worktree.py merge refuses without an APPROVED dd-code-reviewer handoff naming the worktree's exact HEAD sha
context: Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). Q6 asked whether step 4 is machine-required. Today the root map says 'procedure is skill-taught and audit-measured, never gated', while both PRs already require an APPROVED. Recommendation: required — the same kind of lock PRs have, answering the operator's demand for a careful merge; cost: a reviewer round per merge, a one-line bug registration included. Operator: 'Sigo sua orientação e sugestão boa.'
decision: We will make worktree.py merge refuse unless an APPROVED dd-code-reviewer handoff names the worktree's exact HEAD sha. A handoff naming another sha, or any verdict other than APPROVED, is refused.
consequences: + The review checkpoint cannot be skipped or applied to a stale HEAD: any commit after the verdict invalidates it. - Amends the root-map sentence 'procedure is skill-taught and audit-measured, never gated' for worktree merges only; the root map §3 carries the exception. - The lock proves the procedure ran, not the reviewer's honesty — the PR level of assurance. - The refusal's fix line must satisfy the root map's BLOCK law; its form is open in grill round 2.

title: Parallel worktree conflicts: JSONL ledgers merge by union with a duplicate caught by the ledger check; a BACKLOG.json conflict is resolved in the worktree by re-running backlog.py on the rebased tree; TASKS.md markers replay, the most advanced state per line wins
context: Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). Q7 proposed: the append-only JSONL ledgers (BUGS.jsonl, decisions.jsonl, the _histo) merge by union so two parallel appends never conflict, a duplicate caught by the step-3 ledger check; BACKLOG.json is one document, so two parallel additions conflict at rebase and the agent resolves it in the worktree by re-running backlog.py; TASKS.md markers replay, the most advanced state per line wins (round-3 question 1 of the worktrees report). Recommendation added: 'Converter BACKLOG.json para JSONL seria uma mudança maior do que o problema.' Operator: 'Boa sigo sua orientação e sugestão.'
decision: We will resolve parallel-worktree conflicts three ways: JSONL ledgers merge by union and a duplicate is refused by the ledger check at merge step 3; a BACKLOG.json conflict is resolved inside the worktree by re-running backlog.py on the rebased tree, never by hand-merging JSON and never in repos/; TASKS.md task markers replay, and for each line the most advanced state wins. BACKLOG.json stays one JSON document.
consequences: + Parallel bug, backlog and release worktrees merge without manual JSONL conflict resolution. - Union merge accepts a textual duplicate; the ledger check is the only guard against it. - How union is configured without adding a file to the project tree is open in grill round 2 (R2-9).

title: Worktrees are ephemeral and nothing is deleted by time: the doctor flags a worktree or wt/* branch older than one day, an unregistered one and one whose repo left the context; release closure is refused while any wt/* of the repo exists; clean removes only a merged or commit-less worktree
context: Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). Q8 proposed that nothing is deleted by time, since that could lose a commit: the doctor flags a worktree or wt/* branch older than one day, one git does not register, and one of a repo that left the project; release closure is refused while a wt/* of the repo exists (round-3 question 3); clean removes only a worktree whose branch is merged or has no commits, an unmerged branch survives. Operator: 'Sim, sigo a recomendação. Mas atenção. devemos ter orientação clara na sessão para sempre mergear a worktree. E verificarmos worktrees com frequencia e verificar possibilidade de mergear.' On Q3 the operator added: 'não quero worktrees acumulando pois criaremos muitas.'
decision: We will treat every worktree as ephemeral and delete none by time. The doctor flags a worktree or wt/* branch older than one day, a worktree git does not register, and one whose repo left the context. Release closure is refused while any wt/* branch of the repo exists. clean removes only a worktree whose branch is merged or carries no commits; an unmerged branch survives. The session carries clear guidance to always merge the worktree it creates, and open worktrees are checked frequently for whether they can be merged; that mechanism is open in grill round 2 (R2-7).
consequences: + Amends ADR 0099: 'cleaning is the worst case and never deletes a commit' gains its concrete removal and flagging rules. + Accumulation is surfaced every day and blocks closure, never silently reaped. - An abandoned worktree with unmerged commits stays until it is merged or an operator-approved discard; the operator's 'não podemos falhar' on cleanup is measured by the round-2 mechanism.

title: One venv, the workspace's global .dadaia/.venv: the library never builds a venv per worktree; each repo's AGENTS.md names the command that runs its tests inside a worktree

title: Every projected hook carries a timeout (10 s tool lanes, 30 s session lanes); when the deciding pre-gate exceeds its 10 s the harness lets the write through unjudged, a declared fail-open window
context: Bug projected-hooks-carry-no-timeout (fix 2bdff955) made timeout a column of HOOK_DIALECTS: 10 s for tool lanes, 30 s for session lanes, on all six harnesses. Before it, the harness default (600 s) let a slow gate freeze a session for up to ten minutes (the reaper-walk stall of 2026-09-29) but never let a write pass. After it, a pre-gate that runs past 10 s is killed by the harness and the tool call proceeds: no harness offers a fail-closed hook timeout. The group-A review (dd-code-reviewer, CWE-636) asked for this window to be recorded or given a higher ceiling. The gate normally answers in about 0.3 s. Operator ruling 2026-09-29, first-hand, after the explanation: '10 s + ADR (Recommended)'.
decision: We will keep the 10 s timeout on the deciding pre-gate lane like every tool lane and declare its fail-open window: a pre-gate that exceeds 10 s lets that write through unjudged. A pre-gate slower than its timeout is itself a Stall-class bug (CRITICAL), fixed at its cause; the timeout is never raised to hide one.
consequences: + A slow or hung gate can no longer freeze a session (no ten-minute stall). - While a gate is broken slow, file-tool writes pass without the root-whitelist, PROTECTED and scope judgments; the always-on law still forbids those writes. + Records the review MEDIUM on infrastructure/runtime_transforms/hook_wrappers.py as a declared gap, not an open finding.
measured_by: pytest tests/unit/infrastructure/test_runtime_config_session_start.py tests/integration/gate/test_gate_dialects_through_wrappers.py

title: The test wall-clock budget is re-frozen per CI job at the 0.5.0 durations of run 36649988426 (c67b3f09): the growth over 0.4.7 is the new fix-line and onboarding contract coverage, kept after the contract-preserving speedups
context: Bug test-suite-wall-clock-doubled-past-its-frozen-budget (HIGH): dd-test-stewardship PARAMETERS.md freezes the wall-clock budget 'at the current baseline per job'. 0.5.0 ran 2.2x slower than 0.4.7. Speedups landed without weakening any assertion (1c9417df, 137975bc, 2a62128c, 5124c28f, 5ffd58f4, 7fc40fb9): one onboarding world instead of four, tmp source roots, template worlds, in-process first refusals; reviewed APPROVED at c67b3f09. The proposed CLI cold-start speedup was measured and dropped: v0.4.7 185-197 ms vs HEAD 171-181 ms import, --help 0.27 s vs 0.26 s; 0.5.0 is slower because it spawns more real CLI children (about 0.26 s each) in the contract harnesses that prove every BLOCK fix line is one runnable command clearing its refusal (a blocked fix is a CRITICAL Stall). Local -n 3 after the speedups: HEAD 153-178 s vs v0.4.7 86-94 s on a noisy host. CI per-job seconds, v0.4.7 run 35815438821 -> 0.5.0 run 36649988426: Integration 46 -> 115, E2E 54 -> 80, Unit fast 26 -> 46, Unit fast windows 127 -> 137, Unit fast macos 46 -> 82, Contract coverage 53 -> 58, windows 212 -> 255, macos 55 -> 84, Typecheck 24 -> 27, Lint 20 -> 24. decision: We will re-freeze the per-job wall-clock budget at the durations of CI run 36649988426 (feature/0.5.0 at c67b3f09): Integration 115 s, E2E Python 80 s, Unit fast 46 s (windows 137 s, macos 82 s), Contract coverage 58 s (windows 255 s, macos 84 s), Typecheck 27 s, Lint 24 s. From 0.5.0 on, growth past these numbers is again a budget breach judged by dd-test-stewardship; the fix-line and onboarding contract harnesses keep their real process boundaries.

title: A local branch that removing a repo would lose is archived on origin as the tag archive/<branch>/<sha7>, never pushed as a branch; a wt/ branch is never pushed as a branch
context: Bug unrecoverable-fix-line-pushes-a-wt-branch-the-pre-push-refuses (CRITICAL): removing a repo (context dead, repo remove) refuses while a local branch carries commits origin lacks, and its fix line was git push -u origin <branch>, which the pre-push gate refuses for every branch outside the gitflow (a Stall). The first fix (1e631813) archived the tip as a tag on origin; the review (dd-code-reviewer, CHANGES REQUESTED) flagged that it publishes wt/ content against ADR 0097 ('a wt/ branch is never pushed') and the record's expected clause ('merge ... never a push'). Merging into the work branch would bring unreviewed work in against ADR 0110; refusing without a clearing command breaks the Stall law. Operator ruling 2026-09-29, first-hand: 'Arquivar como tag (Recommended)'.
decision: We will make the one lossless exit for a local branch that a repo removal would lose an archive tag on origin: git push origin <branch>:refs/tags/archive/<branch>/<sha7>, one fix line per lost branch, the same for every branch name. A wt/ branch is never pushed as a branch (ADR 0097 amended: 'never pushed' means never as a branch); its normal exit stays the worktree merge ritual (ADR 0109), and the archive tag exists only for a repo removed with the branch unmerged. The pre-push gate judges a ref by what lands on origin: a push onto refs/tags/* is a tag push, a push onto refs/heads/* obeys the branch policy.
consequences: + Removing a repo never loses a commit and its fix line is never refused. + The gate closes the bypass where a local tag pushed onto refs/heads/<principal> skipped branch policy. - wt/ and other local-only work becomes visible on origin as archive tags, still scanned by the denylist and specs-canon checks like every tag. + Supersedes the expected clause 'merge the wt/ branch into the repo's work branch ... never a push of the wt/ branch' of the bug record, which is write-once and stays as history.
measured_by: pytest tests/integration/test_refusal_fix_lines_clear_their_refusal.py -k unpushed_side_branch tests/unit/features/chokepoints/test_push_branch_policy.py tests/integration/test_context_dead_holds.py

title: Open bugs are worked in severity groups and re-evaluated after each group: most severe first, shared root causes fixed together, superseded records closed, never a blind one-by-one pass
context: Operator grill round 2 (remediation release of audit 20260930-structural-convergence), 2026-09-30, answered first-hand in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root). P2: 'Resolvemos os mais graves e vamos resolvendo os medianos e mais simples. a ideia é sempre reavaliar para verificar se o bug não ficou superseeded ... devemos resolver um grupo de bugs e sempre reavaliar os que ficam abertos. E ao tentar resolver bugs mapeados, encontrar bugs que compartilhem a causa raiz ... não podemos listar dezenas de bugs e resolver 1 a 1 cegamente ... devemos classificar criticidade, resolver mais críticos e reavaliar bugs ainda em aberto sempre.' Audit 20260930-structural-convergence measured a 71% same-surface re-bug rate at 3 days under one-by-one fixing.
decision: We will work open bugs in groups ordered by severity: CRITICAL and HIGH first, then MEDIUM with the simple ones alongside, LOW last. Before a group, each bug in it is mapped to its root cause, and every open bug sharing that cause joins the same structural fix. After every group, every still-open bug is re-evaluated against the code as it now is: one whose symptom no longer reproduces is resolved citing the commit that removed its cause; one a decided redesign deletes waits for that redesign. A list of bugs is never fixed one by one in list order.
consequences: + Fixes attack causes, not symptoms; supersessions surface instead of piling up. - Every group costs one re-evaluation pass over the open ledger. dd-bug-resolution and specs/bugs/AGENTS.md teach the order (candidate 5 edits both); it is never gated.
measured_by: dd-audit-project pillar 1 measures the same-surface re-bug rate at every audit; it falls below the 71% of audit 20260930-structural-convergence

ruling.words: Resolvemos os mais graves e vamos resolvendo os medianos e mais simples.

title: worktree.py new derives every worktree from the repo's work branch, creates an impl worktree only on an approved trio, and caps impl at 5 per release and release at 1 per repo and version
context: Operator grill round 2 (remediation release of audit 20260930-structural-convergence), 2026-09-30, answered first-hand in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root). P5 (base = HEAD of feature/<M.m.p>, version from that branch, refusal without a work branch): 'Sim, mapear pontos fortes e pontos fracos dessa solução ... precisamos saber dos riscos e pontos vulneráveis.' P6 (impl refused unless SPEC/PLAN/TASKS are Approved, the check release.py makes in _release_phase.py): 'Isso mesmo. concordo', with the same demand for the risk map. P7 (how many of each kind): 'impl é MAX 5. release definition max 1. bug e backlog podem ser quantos quiser mas são as mais efêmeras, se cria o bug ou backlog, e se mergeia e se deleta. O usuário pode extender a release com release-candidates, se espera o merge ... isso precisa estar bem redondo.'
decision: We will have worktree.py new: (1) branch every worktree from the HEAD of the repo's work branch feature/<M.m.p>, the name taking that branch's version; an associated repo uses its own work branch's version; with no work branch, new refuses with a fix line that creates it. (2) Refuse an impl worktree unless the candidate's SPEC, PLAN and TASKS read Approved on the work branch, judged by the release script's own status parser (ADR 0135), never a second reader. (3) Cap open worktrees: impl at most 5 per repo and release; release at most 1 per repo and version, so a new candidate's definition waits for the previous release worktree's merge; bug and backlog unbounded and ephemeral — create the record, merge, remove in one sitting. Every cap refusal names as its fix the merge or clean of an existing worktree of that kind, never 'wait'. The candidate-5 SPEC carries the strengths, weaknesses and risks of each rule, every weakness with its mitigation or an operator decision.
consequences: + No worktree without a live release; no impl on an undecided definition; bounded parallelism. Risks the SPEC must answer: - a bug found between a promote and the next release definition has no work branch to derive from; - a long-lived worktree drifts and conflicts at rebase (ADR 0128 flags it after one day); - a trio amended after approval leaves in-flight impl worktrees on an older SPEC (the merge judges the SPEC as merged, ADR 0127); - a cap refusal while no open worktree is ready to merge must still carry an executable fix, or it is a Stall; - an associated repo's version can differ from the main repo's release.

title: worktree.py merge checks only the mechanics — clean, allowed set, conflict-free rebase, an APPROVED verdict for the HEAD sha, fast-forward; ledger checks and tests are numbered skill steps; the verdict is a validated handoff
context: Operator grill round 2 (remediation release of audit 20260930-structural-convergence), 2026-09-30, answered first-hand in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root). P8: ADR 0109 step 3 has worktree.py run bugs.py/backlog.py/release.py check, which ADR 0018 forbids (no script calls another); proposal: the ledger checks and tests become numbered skill steps and merge checks only the mechanics. Operator: 'Sim. isso precisa estar bem redondo. não pode haver risco de travamento. E nem de worktrees velhas stale lixo slop.'

title: Every ledger entry is born against the ledger that exists and re-judged at merge: backlog and bugs are correlated before they are written, a release maps every backlog entry, bug and finding it carries both ways; dd-code-review holds the per-kind merge checklist
context: Operator grill round 2 (remediation release of audit 20260930-structural-convergence), 2026-09-30, answered first-hand in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root). P9 (the reviewer's checklist per worktree kind). Operator: 'backlog: ... a cada novo backlog se reveja o backlog já existente para verificar se algum outro registro deve ser atualizado, deletado ... um backlog novo só pode ser criado se em sua concepção ele já considerou o backlog que existia. E o mesmo ao final ao ser mergeado. bugs: ... bugs não podem ser empilhados sem levar em conta outros bugs já existentes em aberto e mesmo fechados recentemente para averiguar reincidência ... antes mesmo de gerá-lo mapear sua correlação com outros bugs. release: ... Se backlog ou bugs ou findings de reports são adicionados em uma release, eles precisam estar claramente mapeados. precisamos saber qual backlog está sendo refletido em uma release e saber quando foi resolvido ou não.'
decision: We will make correlation a precondition of every ledger write and a merge criterion. Backlog: a backlog worktree starts by reading the active backlog and the ADRs; a new entry names every existing entry it updates, obsoletes or relates to, and the same worktree carries the exit of any entry it obsoletes. Bug: before append, the open bugs and those resolved in the last 30 days on the same surface or component are listed, and the new record names the ones it correlates with (or none) and its caused_by; a recurrence of a recently resolved bug says so. Release: every backlog id, bug id and finding id a candidate carries is named in its SPEC Origin, and each record points back — the backlog exit delivered naming the release, the bug's resolved_release, the finding's disposition release — so release.py check lists what is carried, resolved and still open. dd-code-review holds the per-kind merge checklist: backlog (redundant? obsoletes another? contradicts an ADR? operator provenance?); bug (duplicate of an open or recent bug? bug or feature? caused_by right? for a fix: structural cause, RED test, surface delta); release (SPEC coherent with backlog and ADRs; every carried item mapped both ways; a duplicate release or candidate number refused mechanically); impl (three axes and six lenses over the whole SPEC after the sibling impl merges; no task done twice). Each precondition uses the smallest mechanism the candidate-5 PLAN finds, its risks stated.
consequences: + No entry is stacked blind on the ledger; recurrences and duplicates surface at birth. + A release's scope is auditable in both directions. - Every registration pays one read of the ledger. - The 30-day window is a starting value, tuned by the audit.

title: Worktree hygiene is five layers read from git alone: two exits, the same-session merge law, the doctor's per-context list at SessionStart and compaction, release closure and context dead refused while a worktree is open, no Stop hook
context: Operator grill round 2 (remediation release of audit 20260930-structural-convergence), 2026-09-30, answered first-hand in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root). P11 (a deterministic way for no worktree to accumulate; ADR 0112 left the mechanism to round 2). Operator: 'Sim. ta claro.' P17 added: 'se uma spec context project é feita dead, está claro que não deveria sobrar worktree? tudo deve ser mergeado no repo em repos/ ???'
decision: We will keep worktrees from accumulating by five layers, every count read from git (git worktree list, the wt/* branches), never from a second list: (1) two exits only — merge, in the fixed order fast-forward, remove, branch -d, re-runnable after a failure midway; clean, only for a merged or commit-less worktree; (2) an always-on law in the root map: whoever creates a worktree merges it in the same session, and a session ending first names the worktree and why in its handoff; (3) at every SessionStart and compaction the doctor lists the context's open worktrees with kind, age, commits ahead, dirty or clean and ready to merge, a ready one carrying 'fix: worktree.py merge <path>', one older than a day a WARN; (4) release closure and context dead are both refused while any wt/* worktree of the context's repos exists, each refusal carrying the merge or clean fix line — a DEAD context leaves no worktree, everything merged into repos/<r>; (5) no Stop hook (the /goal loop).
consequences: + Accumulation is visible every session and blocks both terminal acts. - A WARN is advice: a session can still ignore it for a day.

title: A worktree holding git-ignored files is never removed silently: merge and clean list them, the operator keeps or drops each, a kept file is copied into repos/<r> still ignored

title: The old worktrees migrate in four steps: remove the eight merged wt/* of dadaia-workspace, archive-tag then discard wt/t-048-01 and -03, triage a consumer context's three worktrees under .dadaia/tmp/wt after a protected-folder check, leave the three in another session's /tmp until the operator confirms
context: Operator grill round 2 (remediation release of audit 20260930-structural-convergence), 2026-09-30, answered first-hand in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root). P15, on ADR 0117's migration. Operator: 'Sim, isso mesmo.'

title: .dadaiaignore judges four places — the workspace root, the .dadaia/ top level, repos/ first level (registered repos only) and worktrees/ (worktrees of ALIVE contexts' repos only); inside the harness directories ADR 0059 holds
context: Operator grill round 2 (remediation release of audit 20260930-structural-convergence), 2026-09-30, answered first-hand in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root). P17: ADR 0092 applies .dadaiaignore to the harness directories, while ADR 0059 (later) judges there only what the install ledger owns. Operator: 'topo, .dadaia. e pasta repos/ no primeiro nível para só permitir repos e na pasta worktrees/ para somente permitir worktrees de repos ALIVE.'
decision: We will apply the root canon and .dadaiaignore at exactly four places: the workspace root's top level; the .dadaia/ top level; repos/ at its first level, where only the repos of registered contexts are canon; and worktrees/, where only worktrees/<r>/<name> of a repo of an ALIVE context is canon. Anything else there is a finding unless an operator glob in .dadaiaignore names it. Inside .claude/, .codex/, .agents/ and the other harness directories ADR 0059 holds: the library judges only what its install ledger owns; 0092's harness-directory clause is void.

context: Operator ruling 2026-09-30, reviewing candidate 5's PLAN: 'existe política clara na definição de PLAN e de TASKS sobre como fazer?? e já equalizado com a lógica de worktrees?? entenda que para habilitarmos paralelismo devemos aqui em PLAN e TASKS trabalhar nisso, ver o que pode ser executado em paralelo para criar lógica de worktrees e merges posteriores.'
