decision: We will plan parallelism in the trio from the keys TASKS already carries, adding no task-line key: (1) each task runs in its own impl worktree (ADR 0106), created only when every task in its blocked-by is merged; (2) two tasks may be open at once only when neither blocks the other and their W: sets are disjoint, except the files merged by union or replay (the JSONL ledgers, TASKS.md markers, ADR 0111); (3) at most 5 impl worktrees are open per release (ADR 0125); (4) PLAN carries a Parallel schedule section: the blocked-by graph as ordered steps, each step listing the tasks that may be open together; (5) merges follow the graph, and each open worktree rebases after a sibling merges (ADR 0109); a conflict outside the union/replay files means the PLAN's write sets were wrong: the PLAN is corrected, never the conflict silently resolved. (6) the schedule is part of authoring, never an afterthought: every step states its planned width (tasks open together) and the PLAN states the critical path (steps from first task to last); at closure the _RELEASE.json log records the measured width per step, the critical path walked and every rebase conflict, planned against actual, so the parallelism strategy is measured candidate by candidate. dd-release-definition §5 and specs/releases/AGENTS.md state this; candidate 5's own PLAN applies it from the task after worktree.py merge lands.

title: No hard line-count limit gates any change: the gate is the architecture principles — DELETE, REBUILD, UPDATE, KEEP, then ADD; no systemic ambiguity or contradiction; clean module boundaries; line counts are a readout
context: Operator ruling 2026-09-30, on candidate 5's +415 production-line estimate and its 'production shrinks' gate: 'não restrinja o trabalho e limites hard de números de linhas adicionados. desde que siga os princípios de arquitetura, de evitar ambiguidade e contradições sistêmicas, de ver o que deletar, atualizar / refazer / reconstruir para então adicionar e manter módulos com arquitetura limpa, não há limite hard coded. eu havia colocado porque vc estava descontrolado. apenas atenção nos princípios que acabei de repetir.' decision: We will gate no change on a line count, production or tests, in any SPEC, task, review or closure. The gate is the principles: every unit walks DELETE, REBUILD, UPDATE, KEEP and only then ADD, and an ADD names what it could not delete or rebuild; no question gets a second decider and no rule contradicts another; modules keep clean, narrow boundaries. The dd-code-reviewer's bug-surface axis judges these. Line counts are measured and logged as a readout only.
consequences: + Needed code (worktree.py) is written at its real size instead of being squeezed or deferred. + Review attention goes to structure, where the bug loop came from. - Without a number, bloat is caught only by review; a review that does not name what an ADD could have deleted has not judged this principle.

title: A skill script reads the gitflow through the CLI's context JSON, never a parser or a hardcoded branch name of its own
context: Operator ruling 2026-09-30 on T-050-96. worktree.py (stdlib, run by system python3) hardcoded `main` in its no-work-branch fix and `feature/` in its work-branch pattern. The operator had ruled: 'MUST come from gitflow, never hardcoded'. The one gitflow reader is GitSubprocessClient.gitflow (ADR 0048). It reads the committed constitution, falls back from an associated repo to its main repo, and parses with PyYAML, so a stdlib script cannot import it. dd-gitflow-default §2a also cuts the work branch from the integration branch, not the principal, so the hardcoded `main` was wrong twice. Options put to the operator: a CLI read (chosen), a stdlib parser owned by the script, or a venv `python -c` import.
decision: We will add the gitflow to the one context record that `context list --json` and `context show --json` render: `gitflow: {principal, integration, work}`, read by the one reader from the main repo. It is `null` when the repo is not on disk. A skill script that needs a branch name runs `<root>/.dadaia/.venv/bin/dadaia context list --json` once and takes the row whose main or associated repo is its target. It never parses the constitution and never names a branch literally. worktree.py derives from it the work pattern `<work><M.m.p>` and, for its no-work-branch fix, `git -C <repo> branch <work><next> <integration>`.
consequences: + One gitflow reader stays; a renamed flow reaches every script. + No new verb (ADR 0018). - Each worktree.py verb costs one CLI start (~0.4s). - A script run outside a workspace with no venv refuses, with the init fix.
measured_by: git grep -nE "'main'|\"main\"|feature/" -- dadaia_workspace/public/skills/dd-gitflow-default/scripts prints nothing; pytest tests/contract/test_cli_output_stability.py tests/integration/test_worktree_new.py

title: Worktree ritual refined by candidate 5 step 3: ready-order merges; a task-fixed bug resolves in a bug worktree; closure runs in its release worktree; one env-only session id; derived behavior-map hashes; .dadaia/mcps/ is operator-owned; the release kind holds the specs law copies
context: Proposed by the main thread from the step-3 reviews and accepted by the operator on 2026-09-30 ('Aceito como está'). Evidence: the fixed in-step merge order held approved worktrees idle (PLAN §5); the impl kind cannot hold BUGS.jsonl (0124), so a task-fixed bug could not close in its fix commit (af538c20 resolved two in a bug worktree); T-050-99's closure hold refused the release worktree closure runs in; T-050-97's first cut read the session id from the payload in the gate and from env in bind, a Stall (the reverted 1a27ae1f); every sibling rebase conflicted only on re-derived hash lines in behavior-map.json; the mcps zone reaps after a day what 0146 (3) says the user keeps; the impl kind cannot hold the specs/*/AGENTS.md copies T-050-103's law changes. A proposal to bind a verdict to `git patch-id` was dropped: it ignores whitespace, and 0106/0127 want the re-review after sibling merges.
decision: We will: (1) merge inside a step in ready order, only true PLAN edges blocking. (2) Resolve a bug a task fixed in a bug worktree holding `specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl` alone, message `chore(bugs): resolve <id>[, <id>] — by <task-id> (<sha>)`; the impl kind never holds BUGS.jsonl, and an Arm B fix keeps 0136's one commit. (3) Run candidate closure in its release worktree; the open-worktree hold excludes the `wt/*` checked out where it runs. (4) Read the session id from the environment only, in gate and bind alike; a nested session that inherits it shares the parent's bind. (5) Treat behavior-map.json hash tuples as derived: a rebase conflict there is resolved by re-recording, like the union and replay files of 0111. (6) Make .dadaia/mcps/ an operator zone, never scanned or reaped. (7) Let the release kind hold the specs/*/AGENTS.md copies.
consequences: + Approved work lands when ready. + No rule forces a hand-edit of a ledger outside its kind. + Closure has a legal home. + Gate and bind cannot disagree on identity; `context bind --print-env` loses its purpose and is deleted. - Nested sessions cannot bind apart without their own DADAIA_SESSION_ID. - Every rebase still needs a review of its sha.
measured_by: pytest tests/unit/core/test_invocation.py tests/integration/test_one_bind.py tests/unit/skills/test_release_implementation_release_script.py tests/contract/test_zone_registry.py tests/contract/test_behavior_map.py tests/integration/test_worktree_lifecycle.py

title: Parallel worktrees only where the PLAN's Parallel schedule declares them; never on the main thread's initiative
context: Operator ruling, 2026-09-30, after the main thread opened three bug worktrees in parallel (a test child-env cluster, a privacy cluster, a bug re-run) that no PLAN scheduled; the privacy one had already edited the ledger scripts T-050-102 was writing. Operator: 'somente é para criar mais de uma worktree para bugs, para impl se estiver claro, bem claro, muito claro, que trabalho pode ser paralelizado sem muitos conflitos no merge ... a condição para diferentes worktrees é dada na etapa de PLAN e impressa nas TASKS de uma release ... somente se pode criar worktrees em paralelo para impl phase se tiver no PLAN e em TASKS, bem dimensionado, seguindo restrições de segurança. Não pode quando der na telha ficar criando worktree.' It narrows 0106 (parallel worktrees allowed) and 0125 (3) (bug and backlog worktrees unbounded), and binds 0141 and 0148 (1). The operator confirmed this scoped decision text on 2026-09-30 ('Confirmo').
decision: We will: (1) open impl and bug worktrees in parallel only for tasks that the PLAN's Parallel schedule places in one step with disjoint `W:` sets (0141), as TASKS prints them; a worktree must never undo what a sibling does. (2) Plan the bugs a release fixes as tasks of its PLAN, scheduled like impl tasks. (3) Open an Arm B fix no PLAN names alone: it is the only bug worktree open, its fix disjoint from every open task's `W:`, else it waits. (4) Open no worktree on the main thread's initiative outside that schedule, except the serial ones: the release worktree (cap 1) that writes a PLAN or its correction, and the registration, backlog or resolve worktree that is the tail of one act. A need the PLAN does not cover goes to the PLAN first.
consequences: + Every parallel merge was measured safe before it started. - Work a PLAN did not foresee waits for a PLAN correction in a release worktree.
measured_by: python3 .agents/skills/dd-release-implementation/scripts/release.py check --specs specs

title: Every release candidate lives in its own rc-N/ folder under specs/releases/<version>/; a release is never flat
context: Operator ruling, 2026-09-30, on finding that release 0.5.0 carried one flat SPEC/PLAN/TASKS trio overwritten by each candidate: "dentro de releases/0.5.0/ teriamos rc1, rc2 rc3 ... não é nem permitido pela minha lei criar uma release plana ... se cria release candidate e se promove ela ... uma release passar a ser extensivel, rc1, rc2, ... rc{n}". The operator chose, 2026-09-30, 'each candidate in rc-N/' over the 0.4.7 shape. Cause: ADR 0019 (operator, Q27 A: 'rc-N stays, one RC defined at a time') was contradicted by ADR 0021, whose acceptance was delegated to an agent in session, and T-047-91 (8999f047) removed rc-N from the law; audit findings 20260930-structural-convergence-F058 and -F061 record the two answers and the overwritten per-candidate slot.
decision: We will: (1) give every candidate of a release its own folder specs/releases/<version>/rc-<N>/ holding that candidate's SPEC.md, PLAN.md and TASKS.md, born there by the definition script and never moved, overwritten or rewritten after its closure; (2) keep only _RELEASE.json at the release root; (3) number candidates 1..n in birth order, the live candidate being the one highest-numbered and not closed; (4) restore release 0.5.0's closed candidates 1-4 from git at their closure commits into rc-1..rc-4, candidate 5 becoming rc-5, the next waves rc-6 onward; (5) promote the release by merging its release PR, as before; the size caps measure one rc-<N>/ trio.
consequences: + A candidate's definition stays readable after it closes; a release grows by candidates without stacking one trio. + Every reader (scripts, doctor, pre-push canon, skills, worktree kinds) resolves one live candidate folder. - Scripts, canon and law that name specs/releases/<version>/{SPEC,PLAN,TASKS}.md change in one task.
measured_by: python3 .agents/skills/dd-release-implementation/scripts/release.py check --specs specs

title: Only the operator accepts a decision: acceptance carries the operator's words, lineage and law deletions are checked, no agent writes accepted
context: Operator ruling, 2026-09-30, after learning that ADR 0021 was accepted by an agent ('delegated to the PM in session') and silently undid the operator's ADR 0019 rc-N ruling: "demita esse agente idiota que violou o que eu falei e violou a ADR. e crie mecanismos claros para isso nunca mais acontecer". The operator approved the five mechanisms as proposed ('Aprovo os 5'), 2026-09-30. The law (specs/ADRs/AGENTS.md §2) already said only the operator accepts; nothing enforced it.
decision: We will: (M1) require every accepted record to carry `ruling: {date, words}` with the operator's verbatim words; the ADR validator (doctor LEDGER-ADR-SCHEMA and tests/contract/test_adr_canon.py) refuses an accepted record without it and refuses acceptance described as delegated or 'in session'; (M2) let a record supersede or amend an accepted record only when it is itself accepted with a ruling; a proposed record never changes another record's status; (M3) make pre-push refuse a pushed commit that deletes a line of a law file (any AGENTS.md or SKILL.md) unless its message cites an accepted ADR; (M4) forbid every role agent (dd-product-engineer, dd-software-engineer, dd-code-reviewer) to write `accepted` or `ruling`; only the main thread transcribes the operator's words, in the turn the operator says them; acceptance is never delegated; (M5) make the canon refuse a flat release (ADR 0150, T-050-109); and retro-audit every accepted record: one whose acceptance has no operator evidence returns to proposed until the operator rules.
consequences: + An operator ruling can only be changed by another operator ruling, and the change is visible in the ledger and the push. + A law line cannot disappear without a cited decision. - Every accepted record needs its ruling backfilled or re-ruled once. - Law-file deletions carry an ADR citation in the commit message.
measured_by: tests/contract/test_adr_canon.py

title: Undo what agents accepted without the operator's order; a published release folder archives whole; SPEC/TASKS size is a soft recommendation
context: Operator ruling, 2026-09-30, on the ADR 0151 retro-audit (agent-accepted records 0001-0004, 0010-0013, 0021, 0024, 0026, 0090, 0091 and the operator rulings they overrode: 0005, 0006, 0007, 0008, 0009, 0014, 0019 Q27). On the archive: 'Restaurar _archive/<v>/'. On size caps: "sem teto rigido. soft teto. recomendação. se tem mais recomenda dividir em mais ... se é grande demais divide em mais de um RC". On the agent-accepted records: "desfaça o que eu não pedi diretamente e agente criou como slop".
decision: We will: (1) at promote, move the whole release folder (_RELEASE.json and rc-1..rc-n) to specs/releases/_archive/<version>/, never delete it (restores ADR 0009/0014's archive; T-050-109); (2) state SPEC.md and TASKS.md size as a recommendation, never a gate: past it, the next work goes into a new rc-<N+1>/ (restores ADR 0143; ADR 0150 (5) and ADR 0010's byte caps no longer bind); (3) return to rejected every record accepted without the operator's order: 0001, 0002, 0003, 0004, 0010, 0011, 0012, 0013, 0024, 0026, 0090, 0091; ADR 0021 keeps only its operator-ruled release-please clause (grill Q6 A) and loses its rc-N/fold/archive retirement (ADR 0150 and (1)); 0015 keeps accepted on the operator's 2026-09-18 words ('Jamais seremos monorepo. No menor caso somos 1 workspace com 1 repo.'); 0022 keeps accepted as the resolution of the operator-confirmed bugs roster-keeps-a-coordinator-persona-while-the-main-thread-coordinates and agent-model-templates-pin-superseded-opus-and-lack-the-economy-template; (4) restore what a rejected record undid of an operator ruling: 0090 removed ADR 0007's doctor-fixable legacy RELEASE.json rename, which returns; where a rejected record undid no operator ruling, its record stops being law and the code it describes is listed at the 0.5.0 publish gate for the operator.
consequences: + Every accepted record traces to the operator's words or an operator-confirmed bug. + A release's history survives publication as a folder. - Law and memory citing the rejected records are rewritten to cite nothing or the operator ruling; the doctor's citation rule measures it.

title: A fix line has two forms: one runnable command, or 'Operator action: <one act>' for an act no command performs; both carry real values and no placeholder
context: batch grill of 2026-10-01 (handoff .dadaia/handoff/dadaia-workspace/2026-10-01T010500Z-main-thread-grill-rc7-rc9-batch.md), D2, carried by 0.5.0 candidate 7. The root map §3 says every BLOCK carries exactly one 'fix: <command>' line, while the code also prints 'Operator action: …' (the id-less session relaunch, SPEC-DOC-048, the registry schema refusals). Open bug fix-lines-are-not-one-runnable-command finds '<ctx>' and 'feature/<M.m.p>' placeholders and fixes that leave the BLOCK in place. ADR 0018's consequences say every fix line names an existing script or verb; ADR 0045 builds the command form only. Operator's answer: 'Aceito D1–D6 (Recomendado)'.
decision: We will amend ADR 0045: a fix line is exactly one of two forms — a runnable command built by the one renderer, whose argv0 exists, or 'Operator action: <one act>' for an act no command performs (accepting an ADR, writing a protected path, relaunching a session). Both carry the real values the site knows and no <…> placeholder. The root map §3 states both forms in its one-fix-line bullet.
consequences: + The law states what the code prints; a placeholder is caught by one harness. - The Operator action form is not machine-runnable; the harness checks only its shape and its real values.

title: diff_direction leaves the bug record and is derived from evidence_diff's prefix; evidence_seam is judged once, by bugs.py resolve, and historic seams stay as written
context: batch grill of 2026-10-01 (handoff .dadaia/handoff/dadaia-workspace/2026-10-01T010500Z-main-thread-grill-rc7-rc9-batch.md), D4, carried by 0.5.0 candidate 7. Open bug bugs-check-trusts-evidence-fields-unverified (F002, F034): bugs.py check exits 0 while BUGS.jsonl lines 653-654 store diff_direction net-negative beside evidence_diff 'net-positive: …', and 15 resolved records name an evidence_seam test node later renamed or merged (the behavior stays covered); the 0.5.0 candidate 6 closure added one moved seam and five pre-rebase SHAs. Both fields are write-once in bug-record-v1; dd-bug-resolution SKILL.md and PILLAR-BUGS.md name the stored key. The ruling narrows the bug's confirmed expected. Operator's answer: 'Aceito D1–D6 (Recomendado)'.
decision: We will delete diff_direction from bug-record-v1 and strip it from every record once, in the change that deletes it; bugs.py check and stats derive the direction from evidence_diff's net-negative|net-positive|net-neutral prefix. bugs.py resolve refuses an --evidence-seam whose file or 'def <name>' does not exist, read with the stdlib; check never re-judges a resolved record's seam, so historic seams and SHAs stay as written. The confirmed expected of bugs-check-trusts-evidence-fields-unverified narrows to: one direction per record, and a seam that exists when it is written.
consequences: + One source for the direction; the 653-654 contradiction cannot recur. + Renaming a test never reddens the ledger. - A seam renamed after resolution goes stale silently; the audit's bugs pillar reads it as history, not as a live pointer. - Every record is rewritten once to drop the key.

title: The SPEC Origin line is one line of clauses 'backlog:<ids>; bugs:<ids>; findings:<ids>', parsed only by release.py; a one-clause line stays valid
context: batch grill of 2026-10-01 (handoff .dadaia/handoff/dadaia-workspace/2026-10-01T010500Z-main-thread-grill-rc7-rc9-batch.md), D5, carried by 0.5.0 candidate 7. A candidate carrying all three kinds names only its backlog pick on the line and maps the rest in an Origin map (0.5.0 candidates 6 and 7), because doctor_release (SPEC-DOC-048) and _backlog_exit each parse the line with their own regex (open bug spec-origin-line-has-two-readers). A one-clause line is the one-clause case of the same grammar, so no closed SPEC changes.

title: worktree.py merge carries an APPROVED verdict across a conflict-free rebase whose patch-id series equals the approved one, in order
context: Operator ruling 2026-10-02 ('Accept, implement in rc-7'), carried by 0.5.0 candidate 7 as T-050-152. ADR 0110 makes worktree.py merge refuse unless an APPROVED dd-code-reviewer handoff names the worktree's exact HEAD sha; worktrees/AGENTS.md §2 step 6: 'A rebase after review changes the sha: review again.' When the work branch moves after the verdict, the rebase onto its tip changes HEAD while every patch stays identical, and each such rebase costs a reviewer round that re-reads the same diff (the T-050-149 and T-050-151 reopen/done chains). ADR 0111 replays TASKS.md markers during that rebase, which does change a patch. The accept act sets amends to "0110" (its decision: the verdict names the exact HEAD sha): ADR 0151 M2 lets only an accepted, ruled record amend an accepted one, so this proposal carries amends null. The same decision changes one more accepted clause, named here because amends holds one id: ADR 0126 (worktree.py merge checks an APPROVED verdict for the worktree's exact HEAD sha).
decision: We will have worktree.py merge accept an APPROVED dd-code-reviewer verdict naming a pre-rebase sha when the rebase was conflict-free and the `git patch-id --stable` series of the rebased work..HEAD equals the approved series in order; any difference, a TASKS marker replay included, requires a review of the rebased sha.
consequences: + A patch-identical rebase onto a moved work branch no longer costs a review round. - A semantic clash with the moved tip is not re-checked at the worktree merge; the manual re-reviews did not check it either, and CI plus the APPROVED verdict on the PR head still gate it. - The accept act sets amends to "0110"; ADR 0110 and ADR 0126 (named in the context, as amends holds one id) both require the verdict to name the worktree's exact HEAD sha; worktrees/AGENTS.md §2 step 6 then reads the carry-over.
measured_by: tests/integration/test_worktree_lifecycle.py: an approved branch whose work branch moved merges after a patch- and message-identical rebase with no new verdict; a hand-resolved conflict, a TASKS marker replay that changes a patch, or a reword refuses for review; an approved sha outside the branch's reflog does not carry over

title: SKILL.md carries a soft and a hard line limit: soft 333 is a dadaia doctor WARNING whose fix line tells the agent to split the SKILL.md into its references/*.md and/or scripts/; hard 500, the Agent Skills format recommendation, stays a contract row; scope SKILL.md only
context: Operator demand 2026-10-02, after the reviewer (finding F3, a bug-proposal skill-md-line-ceiling-survives-adr-0143 that was not registered and is superseded by this record) found that ADR 0143 ('No hard size threshold anywhere') is contradicted by dadaia_workspace/public/entities/behavior-map.json skill_md_line_ceiling 500, enforced by the tests/contract/test_behavior_map.py row every-skill-md-is-within-the-declared-line-ceiling (_find_ceiling_violations). E isso virá uma lei,". Rulings, 2026-10-02: numbers "soft 333 / hard 500 (Recommended)"; scope "Só SKILL.md (Recommended)"; timing "ADR proposed agora + backlog → rc-8 (Recommended)". ADR 0169's 'no ceiling comes back' is untouched: the 500 row never left, and this record declares it law. ADR 0143 itself is unchanged by a proposed record (ADR 0151 M2): the accept act sets amends to "0143", as ADR 0169 did for 0167.
decision: We will declare one size law, for SKILL.md files only, as the single named exception to ADR 0143: (1) soft limit 333 lines — every projected skill's SKILL.md longer than it makes dadaia doctor emit a Severity.WARNING finding SKILL-MD-LENGTH naming the skill and its line count, whose one fix line takes ADR 0158's 'Operator action: <one act>' form with the real SKILL.md path and tells the agent to split that SKILL.md into its skill's references/*.md and/or scripts/; the warning never fails a gate; (2) hard limit 500 lines, the Agent Skills format recommendation (hard 500 = ceil(1.5 × soft)), kept as the existing row every-skill-md-is-within-the-declared-line-ceiling in tests/contract/test_behavior_map.py, which scans the library's skills (dadaia_workspace/public/skills) only; (3) both values live in behavior-map.json (skill_md_line_soft 333 beside skill_md_line_ceiling 500, declared in behavior-map-v1.schema.json) and nowhere else; (4) the CONTEXT-MAP.md skills Budget column (the 6144-byte per-skill budget) is retired, so the 333-line soft limit is the only soft SKILL.md signal; no other file, script, document or corpus gains a limit — every other size stays a soft signal judged by responsibility (ADR 0143). title: context dead never commits: a dirty checkout is refused with a fix line; each sanctioned direct writer commits its own output in the act
context: Operator demand 2026-10-02, workspace replication grill (decisions 1-9, final), backlog context-dead-never-commits (decision 5). Measured at HEAD e83e55783: dead() commits a dirty tree ('chore: auto-sync before dead', features/spec_context/service.py:737-738) and pushes; its preflight carries refusals that exist only for that commit (untracked consent --commit, git identity, the non-work-branch refusal). The commit path is the largest lifecycle bug class (dead-commit-fails-without-git-identity, alive-scaffold-blocks-dead, context-dead-pushes-an-unborn-clone) and contradicts ADR 0105 (repos/<r> receives only merges). ADR 0154 names the sanctioned direct writers (specs/audits/**, context create, the first specs init); at HEAD specs init leaves its output for context baseline to commit and no audits writer commits. ADR 0056 kept dead's non-work-branch refusal on the premise that dead commits and pushes there; the accept act sets amends to "0056" (ADR 0151 M2: a proposed record amends and supersedes nothing).
decision: We will delete dead()'s commit, its --commit flag, its untracked-consent and git-identity refusals and GitSubprocessClient.commit_all; identity_fix stays for baseline and --snapshot. dead refuses a dirty checkout with one fix line per file (move it into a worktree, or discard it) and touches nothing; otherwise it runs the preflight, a fast-forward push of what is committed, the worktree snapshot (ADR 0173) and the hold. The non-work-branch refusal (ADR 0056 g) stays only for unpushed commits on HEAD. Each sanctioned direct writer of ADR 0154 leaves its output committed in the act that writes it.
consequences: + On the default (non-snapshot) path dead commits nothing; the identity, consent and unborn-clone bug paths have no code left there. --snapshot's WIP commit (ADR 0173) is the one commit dead still authors: it stages only the wt/* it archives, never repos/<r>, behind its own identity preflight. + repos/<r> holds only merges and onboarding commits, as ADR 0105 states. - Hand edits in repos/<r> are moved or discarded by the operator before dead. - specs init and the audits writer each gain the commit of their own output.
measured_by: rc-8 AC12.8 case passes: dead on a dirty checkout refuses with one fix line per file and leaves tree and origin untouched; grep -rn commit_all dadaia_workspace returns nothing

title: context dead --snapshot pauses open worktrees: a scanned WIP commit, then an archive/wt tag on origin for a private repo or a local git bundle for a public or unknown one
context: Operator demand 2026-10-02, workspace replication grill (decisions 1-9, final), backlog context-dead-snapshots-open-worktrees (decision 6). Measured at HEAD e83e55783: dead refuses while any wt/* worktree of the context is open (ADR 0128 layer 4; _dead_preflight from worktree_rows and GitSubprocessClient.unrecoverable, infrastructure/git_subprocess.py:244-266), so work in flight cannot be paused; ADRs 0099 and 0128 layer 1 allow two exits only (merge, clean). ADR 0120 archives a lost local branch as the tag archive/<branch>/<sha7> on origin, and the pre-push already scans tags and skips branch policy for them (features/chokepoints/push_gate.py:176-189). Pushing a public repo's WIP would publish unreviewed work. ADR 0112 says nothing is deleted by time, so a local bundle cannot live in the .dadaia/reaped/ TTL hold; operator ruling R1 (2026-10-02) places it in a new durable zone. The accept act sets amends to "0120" (ADR 0151 M2: a proposed record amends and supersedes nothing); this record also narrows ADR 0099 ('always ends merged') and ADR 0128 layers 1 and 4, which the operator rules on at acceptance.
decision: We will add context dead --snapshot. An identity preflight (identity_fix) refuses first, touching nothing. For each open wt/* worktree of the context: a WIP commit on its branch staging only that worktree (untracked files included, ignored files never; never repos/<r>); the denylist plus baseline scan the pre-push runs, a hit refusing with nothing touched; visibility from gh repo view --json visibility, unknown counting as public; a private repo pushes the tag archive/wt/<ctx>/<repo>/<name> to origin, never a branch; a public or unknown repo writes a git bundle at .dadaia/snapshots/<ctx>/<repo>/<name>.bundle with a 'not portable' warning, a new durable zone with no TTL that a bundle leaves only when alive restores it or by an explicit verb, and from which export --hard packs it; .dadaia/reaped/ and the reaper gain no special case; then the worktree is removed. Without --snapshot dead keeps refusing with the merge fix. context alive lists the context's snapshots with the restore fix line in the ADR 0174 layout.
consequences: + Work in flight is paused without a merge and without loss. + Nothing of a public repo leaves the machine. - A third worktree exit beside merge and clean. - A bundle lives on this machine only until a hard export (ADR 0175) carries it. - A new durable zone, .dadaia/snapshots/, joins the zone registry and .dadaia/AGENTS.md. - dead authors one commit again, the WIP commit of --snapshot, so dead-commit-fails-without-git-identity is guarded by the identity preflight. - Visibility needs gh; without it every repo counts as public.
measured_by: the delivering candidate adds: an integration test where dead --snapshot on a private and on a public repo each restores the worktree byte for byte (untracked files included) and pushes nothing of the public one

title: Worktrees live at worktrees/<ctx>/<repo-slug>/<kind>-<M.m.p>-<letter> on wt/<kind>-<M.m.p>-<letter>; kinds by repo role; one name parser; the worktree map stays derived from git
context: Operator demand 2026-10-02, workspace replication grill (decisions 1-9, final), backlog worktree-layout-per-context and context-show-derives-worktrees (decisions 1-3). Measured at HEAD e83e55783: ADRs 0097 (worktrees/<repo>/<M.m.p><letter>) and 0107 (its -<kind> suffix) are both accepted for one shape; the path does not name the context, so the gate, doctor, ctx_inject, closure and the ledger scripts map a path to a context by repo-slug lookup or their own glob; impl reads the trio from the repo it opens in, so an associated repo cannot open impl, and associated repos have no kind rule; kind_for has no production caller; ADR 0112's 'a worktree whose repo left the context' is not implemented. Bug class: sdd-gate-memory-phase-resolves-empty-when-cwd-is-a-linked-worktree-outside-repos, push-gate-own-repo-slug-not-excluded-from-a-git-worktree-outside-repos. The accept act sets supersedes to "0097,0107" (ADR 0151 M2: a proposed record amends and supersedes nothing).
decision: We will place every worktree at worktrees/<ctx>/<repo-slug>/<kind>-<M.m.p>-<letter> on the local branch wt/<kind>-<M.m.p>-<letter>, cut from the repo's work branch, never pushed as a branch (ADR 0120 stands), never under .dadaia/tmp. The letter is the lowest free one per repo and version across all kinds. A main repo opens impl, bug, backlog or release; an associated repo opens impl or bug, and its impl reads the Approved trio of the main repo. context create, alive and repo add create worktrees/<ctx>/<repo-slug>/.gitkeep; dead and repo remove remove it. One name grammar (_NAME_RE) is the only parser and every reader passes through it (the gate's invocation.scope, the ledger scripts' worktree glob, doctor, ctx_inject, closure, rows); kind_for is deleted. ADR 0108 is reaffirmed: the worktree map is derived from git (rows()), never a file; context show --json (one context) renders it per repo with its snapshots, and the doctor and ctx_inject use the same computation; context list --json stays unchanged, the gitflow source rows() reads (ADR 0144); and the doctor reports a worktree whose repo is in no context or whose context is DEAD. Upgrade refuses while any worktree sits in the old layout, with the merge or clean fix.
consequences: + The path names its context: no slug lookup decides ownership. + Associated repos get impl and bug worktrees under the gate. + One parser replaces the readers' own globs and regexes. - Every old-layout worktree is merged or cleaned before upgrade. - ADRs 0114, 0129 and 0132 keep their rules; their worktrees/ path patterns read the new shape through the one parser. - context list --json gains no worktrees field, so rows()' own gitflow read through it never recurses; a caller wanting every context's worktrees asks context show per context.
measured_by: the delivering candidate adds: an integration test where a context with an associated repo opens impl and bug in both repos and the gate scopes both to the context; context show --json, doctor and ctx_inject list the same worktrees

title: Workspace replication: export is read-only, soft (JSON, default) or hard (tar.gz with scanned bundles); init DIR --from <artifact> restores at the artifact's exact version; dadaia import is deleted
context: Operator demand 2026-10-02, workspace replication grill (decisions 1-9, final), backlog export-soft-and-hard and init-from-export (decisions 7-8 and the guiding principle: a workspace is reproduced from one artifact, its state in git, never a local copy). Measured at HEAD e83e55783: export writes contexts and the main repo's branch only and rewrites the registry as a side effect (features/export/service.py:59); it carries no harness and no work in flight; import raises an uncaught KeyError on an incomplete record and turns a null repo_url into 'None'; init re-packs the running distribution with no index (infrastructure/python_env.py:318-360). Scope was narrowed by SPEC 0.4.6 D12/D15 (one fixed spec-contexts.json, tar retired, f4bf7e0b2); no ADR covers export or import. Prerequisites of whoever replicates: the export; PyPI or a private index (UV_INDEX_URL/PIP_INDEX_URL, no code) at the artifact's exact version; access to the listed GitHub repos. This record supersedes SPEC 0.4.6 D12/D15 for the hard export and supersedes no ADR; evals stay out (decision 9).
decision: We will make export read-only. Soft (default): .dadaia/dist/spec-contexts.json, schema v2: contexts (slug, name, state, main repo url, associated [{slug, url}]), the exact dadaia_version, the harnesses of harness_profile.json, per repo its snapshots (archive/wt tags portable; bundles listed as not portable, warning exit). Hard (export --hard): one .tar.gz in .dadaia/dist/ = soft plus the bundles of every open worktree and every bundle of .dadaia/snapshots/, its content passed through the denylist plus baseline scan, a hit refusing; its members are fixed (the soft JSON and snapshots/<ctx>/<repo>/<name>.bundle), validated before extraction (no absolute path, no '..', no link) and extracted only into .dadaia/snapshots/, never the root. Neither carries the denylist, credentials, sessions or the install ledger. init DIR --from <artifact> refuses a version other than the artifact's with the fix 'uvx dadaia-workspace==<v> init DIR --from <file>', installs its harnesses, registers its contexts DEAD through the one register, checks each repo with git ls-remote and lists the unreachable ones, extracts a hard artifact's bundles into .dadaia/snapshots/<ctx>/<repo>/, where alive restores them, and prints the context alive fix for each context ALIVE in the artifact. dadaia import is deleted; re-running init is the upgrade, so --from serves a new and an existing workspace.
consequences: + One artifact and one command replicate a workspace for a teammate or a new machine, at an imposed version. + Export stops mutating the registry. + One registration path (register) instead of import's own. - A hard artifact holds unpushed work: scanned, but its custody is the operator's. - The memory atom context-portability is rewritten. - Two artifact schemas ship.
measured_by: the delivering candidate adds: a clean-container test running init --from on a soft and on a hard artifact, then context alive, then doctor with no finding; a hard export with a planted secret refuses; both artifacts validate against their schemas

title: Nine principles whose test leaves pytest keep a check: seven named checks of the one guard-script CI job, P-07 and P-28 their own tool; P-30 loses its false archive clause
context: Review re-reviews of the rc-8 SPEC at fb8a29a75 (findings H2 and M6) and at 196f611aa (HIGH-A, MEDIUM-A, MEDIUM-B, LOW-C), 2026-10-03. rc-8 AC8.3 (backlog meta-tests-leave-pytest; ADRs 0163, 0166, 0167) takes out of pytest the files that measure QUALITY P-21, P-22 and P-28 (tests/contract/test_stewardship_mechanics.py), P-23 (test_test_suite_ratchets.py) and P-33 (test_ci_workflow_hygiene.py -k model_api, a selector the case id model-api-call does not match: audit F131), and ARCHITECTURE P-07 and P-10 (test_import_linter_ignore_cap.py), P-30 (test_ci_workflow_hygiene.py, the release-please cases of test_release_semver_canon.py, test_version_lineage_consistency.py) and P-32 (test_memory_canonical_shape.py, beside the retired doctor rule RELEASE-TREE-MEMORY: audit F128). P-30's clause 'a candidate's closed trio lives in git at its CLOSURE commit, never in a copied candidate or archive directory' is false: accepted ADR 0152 (1) restored the archive, and release.py ship moves the whole release folder to specs/releases/_archive/<version>/; 0152 (3) left ADR 0021 only its release-please clause. QUALITY P-29 (test_docs_derived_from_memory.py) is left out: it cites ADR 0012, rejected by 0152 (3), and its fate is check #7 of the 0.5.0 publish-gate audit (specs/audits/20260930-050-publish-gate-baseline/AUDIT.md §6), owned by rc-12; a ### P-NN line never takes the ADR 0138 lane, so its file stays in pytest until the operator rules there. A principle needs an existing check that fails when violated and changes only in the commit carrying its accepted ADR (specs/memory/AGENTS.md §1-§2). ADR 0167's consequences routed P-21, P-22, P-23 and P-28 to the meta-test CI job and the others to owner files once tests/contract/ dissolves; moving their files to guard scripts at rc-8 changes that route. This record amends 0167; its amends field is written at acceptance, because a proposed record never names an accepted one (ADR 0151 M2, doctor LEDGER-ADR-SCHEMA). Operator ruling 2026-10-03 on the rc-8 SPEC amendment (AskUserQuestion, 'Use the native tools (Recommended)'): P-07 and P-28 are measured by the tool itself, not by guard checks. import-linter 2.13 expands modules = dadaia_workspace.features.* in an independence contract (checked 2026-10-03: kept on the tree, broken by a planted sibling import), and pytest --strict-markers refuses a mark absent from pyproject.toml's markers (not yet in addopts; the suite collects under it).
decision: We will measure nine principles: seven by named checks of the one guard-script CI job (its script path is the one the rc-8 PLAN declares), each with a planted violation that turns the job red, and two by their own tool. QUALITY: P-21 tier-timeout (a test without its tier timeout, or with an overridden explicit timeout); P-22 quarantine-needs-bug (a quarantine mark without bug= refuses collection, and every gating selector in .github/workflows excludes the lane); P-23 private-import-ratchet (its ceiling lives in the script); P-28 by pytest --strict-markers in pyproject.toml's addopts, which refuses any mark absent from its markers list, flaky and quarantine among them (conftest _KNOWN_MARKERS and its equality test leave); P-33 no-model-api-in-ci. ARCHITECTURE: P-07 by lint-imports alone, contract features-no-cross-feature listing modules = dadaia_workspace.features.*, which covers every features package (setup.cfg's hand-kept list and its equality test leave); P-10 ignore-cap (the cap lives in the script); P-30 release-workflow-canon (the release workflow, the release-please manifest and config, the pyproject version equal to the CHANGELOG's top dated section); P-32 memory-canonical-shape, beside doctor rule LINT-1. Each statement stays and only its Measured by line changes, plus the 'test module is the numeric home' wording of P-10 and P-23, which names the guard script; P-07 and P-10, pre-canon, carry ADR: 0176 from that commit (specs/ADRs/AGENTS.md §5). Two exceptions: P-28's statement drops _KNOWN_MARKERS, the marker list's one source being pyproject.toml; and P-30's statement loses its clause 'a candidate's closed trio lives in git at its CLOSURE commit, never in a copied candidate or archive directory', its Rationale loses the hand-copied archive, and its ADR line names this record, because ADR 0152 (1) archives a shipped release into specs/releases/_archive/<version>/. This record does not change QUALITY P-29, its ADR line or its check, and rules nothing on ADR 0012 or publish-gate check #7.
consequences: + No principle loses its check when its test leaves pytest; audit F128 and F131 close with the P-32 and P-33 hunks; P-30 states what release.py ship does. + One route for every meta-test principle instead of 0167's two. + P-07 and P-28 keep no list in sync: a new features package or marker is covered by the tool itself. - The operator accepts this record in the rc-8 release worktree, in the commit that carries the nine ### P-NN hunks, once the guard script exists (specs/ADRs/AGENTS.md §3). - The non-principle lines naming what rc-8 removes (QUALITY.md Test architecture and Gates, ARCHITECTURE.md Tech Stack and the features package map) take their ADR 0138 truth correction at or before that commit, with ARCHITECTURE.md Structure's import-linter contract count (seven stated, six in setup.cfg); an impl task re-derives the QUALITY markers of docs/bug-ledger-lessons.md after the last QUALITY.md edit (precedent T-050-150). - Accepted records whose measured_by names a test file rc-8 moves or deletes (0016, 0017, 0020, 0021, 0023, 0025, 0049, 0052, 0070, 0071, 0078, 0080, 0088; 0080 keeps tests/unit/core/test_workspace_layout_zones.py, which asserts no .cache zone, and swaps tests/unit/features/ci_preflight/test_no_pollution.py for the no-cache-in-tree case tests/integration/test_tool_caches_stay_in_the_tmp_zone.py, which gains a pytest row) are repaired in place under ADR 0138, each by a chore(adrs): repair commit in the release worktree right after the moving task merges, because an impl worktree cannot stage decisions.jsonl (precedent a6bca8d52). - P-29 keeps a pytest check and a rejected ADR until rc-12 rules publish-gate check #7.
measured_by: the guard-script CI job's log names the seven checks, each red on its planted violation; lint-imports --config setup.cfg --no-cache and pytest --collect-only -q exit 0, and each fails on a planted sibling-feature import or unregistered mark; awk '/^## /{p=($0=="## Principles")} p' specs/memory/ARCHITECTURE.md specs/memory/QUALITY.md | grep -nE 'test_(stewardship_mechanics|test_suite_ratchets|import_linter_ignore_cap|ci_workflow_hygiene|memory_canonical_shape|release_semver_canon)|_KNOWN_MARKERS|RELEASE-TREE-MEMORY|model_api|archive directory' prints nothing

title: Only an evals repo may call a model API in CI, only in workflow_dispatch or schedule jobs; a context's main repo and its other associated repos never do (scopes the map's section 3 line and ADR 0025)
context: Operator demand 2026-10-03: agent-behavior evals gate the 0.5.0 publish (backlog agent-behavior-evals); measuring what an agent does needs a model call. The root map section 3 ('no CI job calls a model API', shipped from dadaia_workspace/public/data/AGENTS.md), dd-gitflow-default SKILL.md section 3b, CICD-AUTOMATION.md, QUALITY.md P-33 and the sdd-gate-v3 atom state it for every CI job; ADR 0025 made it law after a lib PR security-review job failed closed for want of a model secret. Grill Q11 (2026-10-03) put model calls in a separate repo; the grill handoff 2026-10-03T163043Z-main-thread-grill-evals-050 (final) made dadaia-evals public (free Actions minutes) on four conditions; grill round 2 (handoff 2026-10-03T170932Z-main-thread-grill-evals-format) chose Harbor as the runner, whose jobs/ tree (trial logs and transcripts) is the uploaded artifact. On a public repo a pull_request job runs fork code, a pull_request_target job hands that code the secrets, and a self-hosted runner executes it on the operator's machine. The accept act sets amends to "0025" (ADR 0151 M2: a proposed record amends and supersedes nothing).
decision: We will scope the rule by repo role inside a context: (1) a context's main repo and every associated repo but an evals repo run no CI job that calls a model API - for this context the main repo is the library, and ADR 0025's workflow scan stands unchanged as check no-model-api-in-ci of the library's guard-script CI job (ADR 0176); (2) an evals repo - an associated repo whose one role is to measure agent behaviour against the distribution its context ships, a term the delivering candidate defines in CONTEXT.md - may call a model, only in jobs triggered by workflow_dispatch or schedule, never push, pull_request or pull_request_target; (3) an evals repo uses no self-hosted runner; (4) the model secret is read only by those jobs, at job level; (5) uploaded artifacts and transcripts come only from synthetic projects built inside the run, never from the operator's repos or workspace; (6) every uploaded artifact (the runner's jobs/ tree included) and the job summary pass a secret scan whose patterns include the model secret's own value, run before any upload and before the summary is written; a hit fails the job closed and uploads nothing. The map line becomes: no CI job of a context's main repo or associated repos calls a model API, except an evals repo's, under (2)-(6). The change ships from dadaia_workspace/public/data/AGENTS.md with SKILL.md section 3b, CICD-AUTOMATION.md and the sdd-gate-v3 atom aligned; P-33's statement is re-scoped the same way and names this ADR, its check staying no-model-api-in-ci.
consequences: + Agent behaviour is measured in CI with no model secret in the library or on any PR path. + A public evals repo costs no Actions minutes. - Model-calling jobs exist in the context, in a repo the library's workflow scan does not read: the evals repo carries its own scan. - Grill Q15's self-hosted fallback for the Devin login closes; a failed spike leaves Devin local-only. - A false scan hit fails a paid run. - The shipped map text changes; every instance re-projects.
measured_by: the delivering candidate adds: in the evals repo, a check failing when a workflow that reads the model secret has a trigger other than workflow_dispatch or schedule, a non GitHub-hosted runs-on, the secret at workflow level, or an upload step or job-summary write not preceded by the secret scan step, plus that scan run on a fixture tree holding a planted token value exiting non-zero; in the library, check no-model-api-in-ci of the guard-script CI job (ADR 0176) stays green

title: 0.5.0 publishes only after the operator reads a dadaia-evals gate verdict: a paired drop against 0.4.7 or T1 below 3/3 blocks; an evals/gate status required by approve waits for 0.5.1
context: ADR 0122 makes 0.5.0's gate zero open bugs, backlog and findings, and the D1-D10 first-run rubric a readout, never a gate. Operator 2026-10-03: evals must protect 0.5.0 before PyPI (many behaviour changes; 0.4.7 downloads doubled). The grill handoff 2026-10-03T163043Z-main-thread-grill-evals-050 (final) answered 'Manual read (Recommended)' and 'Paired drop + T1 3/3 (Recommended)'; grill Q6 kept regression tasks gating and capability tasks readout. Two tasks at k=3 are noisy: one trial's difference is no signal, a task falling from >=2/3 to <=1/3 is. T1 cold onboarding is the surface 0.5.0 rc-1 rewrote and the first one a new user meets. The release.yml approve job gates the build of the tag release-please mints after the promote PR merges, so that tag sha does not exist while the work branch can still log; its tree differs from the promote PR head only by the files release-please writes - CHANGELOG.md, .release-please-manifest.json and the version line of pyproject.toml (the 0.4.7 release commit 2d1f4351a touched exactly these). The promote PR head still carries the pre-bump version (pyproject.toml version = 0.4.7, the PyPI baseline's own), and that version is the wheel's distribution_version, which capabilities reports and reconcile and certify read. The accept act sets amends to "0122" (ADR 0151 M2: a proposed record amends and supersedes nothing).
decision: We will: (1) dispatch dadaia-evals eval.yml on the evaluated sha - the promote PR head, the integration tip the pre-staged ship verdict names - before the promote PR merges; it runs T1 (cold onboarding) and T2 (seeded bug, Arm B), k=3 each, on dadaia-workspace 0.4.7 from PyPI and on the wheel built from that sha, after eval.yml stamps the version release-please-config.json's release-as names (0.5.0) into pyproject.toml's version line before uv build, so the candidate wheel carries the version its tag will; (2) block the publish when a task passing >=2/3 on 0.4.7 passes <=1/3 on the candidate, or T1 passes fewer than 3/3 on the candidate; (3) hold every other result, T3 included, as readout; (4) have the operator read the verdict from the job summary and its artifact, and log the run, its verdict and the evaluated sha in the work branch's _RELEASE.json before the promote PR merges; (5) at the release.yml approve job (environment release-gate) approve only when git diff --name-only from the evaluated sha to the release tag lists nothing outside CHANGELOG.md, .release-please-manifest.json and pyproject.toml, and the pyproject.toml hunk changes only its version line; otherwise dispatch eval.yml on the tag sha first and approve only on a non-blocking verdict; release.yml does not change in 0.5.0, and a commit status evals/gate required by approve is deferred to 0.5.1 (backlog evals-release-gate-status). This amends ADR 0122 only as far as these regression tasks gate; its zero-open gate and the D1-D10 readout stand.
consequences: + An onboarding or bug-flow regression cannot reach PyPI unseen. - The read is manual: a skipped read goes unenforced until 0.5.1. - A flaky T1 blocks; the operator re-runs or rules. - Twelve trials per gate run, billed to the operator's plan credit (ADR 0177, grill Q14).
measured_by: the work branch's _RELEASE.json log, in a commit that precedes the promote PR merge, names the dadaia-evals eval.yml run, its verdict and the evaluated sha, and that sha equals the promote PR head; git diff --name-only from the evaluated sha to the 0.5.0 release tag lists only the release-please file set of decision (5) with pyproject.toml changed only in its version line, or a dadaia-evals eval.yml run whose lib-ref input is the tag sha has a non-blocking verdict (the Actions run is the record)

title: Agent-behavior evals return without the plugin: a harness-neutral associated repo runs them against the shipped wheel, reopening the 2026-09-20 rejection of plugin-packaging-and-skill-evals
context: Backlog plugin-packaging-and-skill-evals (one Claude plugin plus claude plugin eval in CI) exited rejected on 2026-09-20 (grill Q13/Q14): a Claude-only plugin contradicts the universal .agents/skills channel (ADR 0017). Its eval half fell with the packaging, and nothing has measured agent behaviour since. Operator demand 2026-10-03 makes evals gate 0.5.0; the rejection's reason holds for the packaging, not for the measurement.
decision: We will measure agent behaviour from the dadaia-evals repo, associated to the dadaia-workspace context, against the distribution a user installs - the wheel uv build makes from a library ref, or the PyPI release - read through the universal surface every harness reads. No plugin and no second distribution is built, and the library ships no eval code. Claude Code is the first harness (0.5.0); others join through the backlog (evals-harness-lanes-and-benchmark). title: Ledgers merge by plain git 3-way: an overlapping ledger change refuses at rebase and is redone by the ledger's own writer on the rebased tree; no union merge and no dedupe check, reversing the union clauses of ADRs 0111, 0129 and 0141
context: Bug worktree-merge-union-duplicates-ledger-records-on-in-place-mutation (HIGH, operator-confirmed 2026-10-03). ADR 0111 classed the JSONL ledgers as append-only ('JSONL ledgers merge by union and a duplicate is refused by the ledger check at merge step 3'), ADR 0129 had worktree.py new write the union line ('new writes the union-merge lines'), and ADR 0141 (2) and (5) exempt 'the files merged by union'; T-050-95 (152da630e) and T-050-98 (36ce79d7d) shipped *.jsonl merge=union in .git/info/attributes. But BUGS.jsonl, decisions.jsonl and FINDINGS.jsonl records change in place (an ADR accept, a status flip, an ADR 0138 measured_by repair, bugs.py update and resolve, audit.py disposition), and union replays a changed line beside the old one: the rebase exits 0 with the id twice (ADRs 0177-0179 doubled on wt/0.5.0a-backlog). The step-3 ledger check never existed: _worktree_end.merge runs no ledger check after its rebase. The fix under rework in bug worktree 0.5.0d-bug stops writing the line, with no migration (no published release wrote it: v0.4.7 and main carry no _worktree_new.py; the main thread deletes it by hand once from the three pre-release repos that hold it), and lets a ledger conflict refuse at rebase with fix: git -C <tree> rebase <work>, adding no dedupe layer - a departure from accepted text. Main thread to the operator, 2026-10-03: 'The union-ledger fix departs from accepted ADRs 0111/0129. Which direction?' Operator: 'Remove union (Recommended)'. The writer re-run is stated today only in the _worktree_end.py _rebase docstring (lines 130-131). The accept act sets amends to "0111,0129,0141" (ADR 0151 M2: a proposed record amends nothing) and, in the ADR 0138 repair lane, repoints ADR 0111's measured_by, whose first test the fix renamed (test_parallel_siblings_union_ledgers_and_replay_task_markers -> test_parallel_siblings_replay_task_markers) and whose union clause it deleted, to: pytest tests/integration/test_worktree_lifecycle.py::test_parallel_siblings_replay_task_markers tests/unit/skills/test_bug_resolution_bugs_script.py::test_duplicate_ids_are_refused (TASKS.md markers replay, most advanced state wins; bugs.py refuses a duplicated id; the BACKLOG.json re-run is agent procedure, measured by no test); it repoints ADR 0129's measured_by to name tests/integration/test_worktree_new.py::test_new_branches_and_locks explicitly (new locks with the dadaia: reason), dropping its .git/info/attributes clause - that assert lived in test_worktree_new.py, which the fix deleted while renaming the test; and it repoints ADR 0141's measured_by so 'outside the union/replay files' reads 'outside TASKS.md and the JSONL ledgers'. The measured_by test below lands with a fix still under rework: the accept act re-verifies it exists and passes on the work branch.
decision: We will merge every ledger by plain git 3-way merge - BUGS.jsonl, decisions.jsonl, every FINDINGS.jsonl, every _histo.jsonl and BACKLOG.json alike: no merge driver, no union, no dedupe step. worktree.py new writes nothing into .git/info/attributes. A rebase in which both sides changed overlapping ledger lines refuses with fix: git -C <tree> rebase <work>, and the agent resolves it inside the worktree with the ledger's own writer: (1) run the fix line; the rebase stops at the conflicted commit; (2) per conflicted ledger, git -C <tree> checkout --ours -- <ledger> (in a rebase, ours is the work branch), dropping this branch's version; (3) redo that commit's ledger act on it through the ledger's writer - bugs.py for specs/bugs, backlog.py new or exit for specs/backlog, audit.py for specs/audits, and for decisions.jsonl, which has no script, the same one-record append or in-place edit re-made by its author (the main thread for an accept); (4) run that writer's check, git add <ledger>, git rebase --continue; (5) the rewritten commit takes a fresh dd-code-reviewer verdict on the rebased sha unless its patch-id series is unchanged (ADR 0168), then worktree.py merge re-runs. Conflict markers are never hand-merged and nothing is resolved in repos/<repo>. After this record is accepted, backlog worktree-memory-states-plain-ledger-merge states the procedure as the law line of worktrees/AGENTS.md step 7 (source dadaia_workspace/public/data/worktrees-AGENTS.md line 30), since changing a law line needs an accepted ADR (ADR 0151 M3); until then this record and the _worktree_end.py _rebase docstring carry it, and the bug fix leaves that law line untouched. ADR 0141 (2) and (5) read 'TASKS.md markers (replayed) and the JSONL ledgers (redone by their writer)' where they said 'the files merged by union or replay': the ledgers stay exempt from the W: disjointness check. ADR 0111's TASKS.md marker replay and BACKLOG.json writer re-run stand.
consequences: + A ledger record lands once or the rebase refuses; no silent duplicate, and no check is needed to catch one. + One merge path for every ledger: the union attribute, its idempotent write and the missing step-3 check leave, with no migration code. - Two parallel worktrees appending to one ledger now conflict at rebase where union merged them; the writer re-run costs a rebase stop and, usually, a fresh review. - decisions.jsonl has no writer script: its redo is a hand re-application by the record's author.
measured_by: pytest tests/integration/test_worktree_ledger_conflict.py::test_in_place_ledger_change_refuses_at_rebase (an in-place ledger change in a worktree against an append on the work branch refuses at rebase with fix: git -C <tree> rebase <work>)

title: worktree merge lands exactly the verified, approved HEAD: it runs the repo's declared verification command on that HEAD and never rewrites; a moved work branch refuses with a rebase fix line
context: Grill 2026-10-04 (.dadaia/handoff/dadaia-workspace/2026-10-04T190000Z-main-thread-grill-fix-induced-bugs.handoff.json) after a read-only audit at 76d7af604: 18 fix-induced breaks reached feature/0.5.0 unregistered, because merge ran no test and CI ran only after the push. Every worktree-merge bug sits on merge's rewrite step invalidating its own authorization: first-approved-overrides-newer-rejected, linearizes-a-branch-already-containing-work, union-duplicates-ledger-records, and the rejected rewrites-the-branch-before-refusing. That rewrite is the in-merge rebase plus TASKS-marker replay of worktrees/AGENTS.md §2 step 6 and ADR 0111's TASKS clause. ADR 0168 (a verdict carried across a patch-identical rebase) and ADR 0180 (ledger conflicts redone by their writer inside the worktree) stand. Library users work in any language. ADR 0109 step 2 ('rebase onto the repo's work branch' as a merge step) and ADR 0126 (merge verifies 'the rebase onto the work branch has no conflict', and 'the repo tests are numbered steps of the merge ritual … run by the agent before merge') carry the rewrite and leave verification to the agent.
decision: We will make worktree.py merge: refuse dirty, check the allowed set, require the work branch to be an ancestor of HEAD, require the approval of HEAD (ADR 0168 carry-over stands), run the verification command the repo declares — read from the HEAD being landed — and refuse on non-zero, then fast-forward. A repo with no declaration is refused with one fix line naming where to declare it. When the work branch has moved, merge refuses with fix: git -C <tree> rebase <work>; merge never rebases, replays markers or rewrites. This amends ADR 0126 (merge's rebase clause and its 'verify by itself only / tests run by the agent' clause), ADR 0109 step 2 (which 0126 amends), ADR 0111's TASKS clause, and worktrees/AGENTS.md §2 step 6. For dadaia-workspace the declared command is one repo script running every Linux job of ci.yml, which ci.yml itself calls.
consequences: + Nothing lands unverified; the 18-break escape path closes at the merge, before the push. + The rewrite path and its reflog search, ordering rule, already-contains special case and cross-skill reach-in are deleted. + One step for every worktree kind, no flag, any language. - Each repo declares its command once. - A worktree can weaken its own declared command; the reviewer sees it in the diff. - A landing runs the full Linux suite locally; Windows/macOS stay CI-only and are declared unverified in the verdict.
measured_by: pytest tests/integration/test_worktree_lifecycle.py::test_merge_lands_only_what_the_declared_verify_command_passes tests/integration/test_worktree_lifecycle.py::test_a_moved_work_branch_refuses_and_its_fix_rebase_keeps_only_an_identical_patch (a non-zero declared command refuses and lands nothing; no declaration refuses with one fix line; a worktree whose own commit adds the declaration lands; a moved work branch refuses with the rebase fix line and leaves both branches untouched)

title: A break caused by an already-merged fix is a bug with caused_by naming a bug or a task; it stops the line and is redone as a REBUILD — one commit holding the culprit's revert and the smallest correct redo; lineage blame skips no refactor commit
context: Grill 2026-10-04 (.dadaia/handoff/dadaia-workspace/2026-10-04T190000Z-main-thread-grill-fix-induced-bugs.handoff.json). The audit at 76d7af604 found 18 fix-induced breaks landed as unregistered follow-up commits: specs/bugs/AGENTS.md §1 ('NOT a bug: your own mistake'), dd-release-implementation §2a ('a red job is fixed at its cause') and the absent task form of caused_by let them bypass ADR 0164's lineage, so LINEAGE rule 6 never fired; caused_by refused task ids, and blame skipped refactor commits and tests/. Research cited in the grill: size and scatter predict fix-induced bugs, the kernel reverts the culprit first, agents game tests by editing them.
decision: We will: (1) limit the 'own mistake' exclusion to unmerged rework inside a worktree; a break caused by a merged fix is always registered with caused_by, and caused_by accepts a bug or a task id (amends ADR 0164 (3)); (2) make one fix-induced bug, going forward — a caused_by other than none now means a REBUILD, amending ADR 0164 (5) — stop work in flight until its REBUILD lands; a REBUILD is one commit holding the culprit's revert and the smallest correct redo, shaped refactor(<task-id>): REBUILD <unit> — … or refactor(bugs): <id> — REBUILD <unit>: …, and bugs.py fix finds the latter; (3) route a red caused by a merged fix to Arm B, never a follow-up commit; (4) drop the refactor skip from resolve's blame (amends ADR 0164 (2), after ADR 0183) and let test-file lines yield candidates; (5) rewrite the law files rc-8 touches once, positive by default, a prohibition kept only with its demonstrated failure as a short reason or bug/ADR id, and the reviewer's verdict carrying the repo's declared verification command's output.
consequences: + Fix-induced bugs are counted, so LINEAGE's REBUILD trigger can fire. + A REBUILD's lines stay blamable. + Law text no longer sanctions a follow-up commit. - A stop-the-line pause costs throughput. - More blame candidates to dismiss, each with a lineage reason. - Past fixes are not rebuilt retroactively (Q18): only the surfaces the audit ruled.
measured_by: T-050-192's cases pass, delivered in rc-8: bugs.py resolve accepts --caused-by T-NNN and proposes a refactor(T-…) commit as a candidate (tests/unit/skills/test_bug_resolution_bugs_script.py::test_resolve_proposes_caused_by_by_blame, ::test_caused_by_names_a_task_some_tasks_file_carries); bugs.py fix <id> finds a refactor(bugs): <id> — REBUILD commit (tests/unit/skills/test_bug_resolution_bugs_script.py::test_fix_derives_each_fix_commit_and_its_direction); rc-9's cases pass for what grill 2026-10-05 Q21 carried there (rc-8 SPEC §Carried): AC9.3's and AC12.1–AC12.3's law, AC12.12's law and reviewer rows, and AC12.4, where bugs.py status --all shows the 27 retro records with their expected status; the next audit's PILLAR-BUGS readout shows every fix-induced record in its window with caused_by other than none and a REBUILD commit

title: A bug record carries found_in, stamped at registration; introduced_in is derived on read, never typed; a record leaves the ledger only by an accepted ADR
context: Grill 2026-10-05 (.dadaia/handoff/dadaia-workspace/2026-10-05T005326Z-main-thread-grill-bug-window-review.handoff.json) G1, G6, G12; rc-8 SPEC W13 AC13.1, AC13.6 (operator-approved 2026-10-05). Operator, G1: '1. quando o bug foi identificado. e 2. quando a implementação que gerou o bug ocorreu. acredito que seja achado e nascido.' Rulings 2026-10-05: 'Release certa, rc 'unknown' (Recommended)'; 'Ficam arquivadas, ADR retroativa (Recommended)'. The age path archived 65 records at the 0.4.7 ship with no decision naming why; --resolved-release is hand-typed.
decision: We will: (1) stamp found_in {release, rc} once at registration from one function instant -> candidate: the release whose _RELEASE.json span (first log entry to shipped.ts) holds the instant, the rc from the commit adding one rc-N/SPEC.md alone whose status reads non-Approved, else rc unknown; a shallow clone is refused; resolved_release comes from the same function and --resolved-release leaves; (2) derive introduced_in on read from caused_by's culprit commit instant, never typed, stored only by a class ruling where no culprit derives it, a derivable culprit winning; (3) let a record leave BUGS.jsonl only by bugs.py archive --adr <id> naming an accepted ADR, recorded as archived_by, in a commit chore(bugs): archive <ids> — ADR <id>; the age path (--threshold-days, --now, archivable, SPEC-DOC-041) is deleted; (4) restore the 65 records age-archived at the 0.4.7 ship in one commit, the one-time writer exception.

title: Gates per task, stage and job; one review per job; the task is the dispatch unit
context: rc-8 paid the full scripts/ci.py (~6 min) at every worktree merge (gate 1, 0185), a review per worktree and a dispatch per micro-step; the operator measured the ritual wait as the main cost ('na proxima RC é 100% obrigatorio demolir essas inficiencias'; 'rc-9 não deve ter ritual velho, nada dele'). rc-9 SPEC Job 1 demolition (a), (c), (e); grill 2026-10-05 T040135Z, T045010Z, T050738Z.
decision: scripts/ci.py has three levels: task (ruff, mypy on touched files, owner tests), stage (lint, mypy, guards but drift, unit, integration) and job (the full command plus the CI matrix). A task fast-forwards onto its job branch after its gate; a stage closes with no task worktree open and its gate green; a job merge runs the job level once and needs one APPROVED verdict naming its green CI-matrix run. No review at a task or stage merge, except one per stage past 400 added lines. The task is the dispatch unit; the job driver's own edit lands as a task. The verify: line and its shell=True run leave.
consequences: + One full CI run and one review per job instead of per merge; the ritual wait drops by an estimated 75–80% (rc-9 AC1.7). - A defect inside a stage is caught at the stage or job gate, not at each task merge.
measured_by: rc-9 AC1.1, AC1.2 and AC1.4 cases (test_ci_script.py levels; job merge refuses without a verdict naming the matrix run; task merge lands with no verdict)

title: One worktree tree per job; no worktree kinds and no kind allowed sets
context: The four kinds (0106) split one change across worktrees: the rc-8 closure deadlocked because the release kind could not write derived docs and the impl kind could not write memory. 0125's impl-only-on-approved-trio and 0124's specs-only-by-merge rules assumed the kinds. rc-9 SPEC Job 1 demolition (b).

title: No rc ever closes with an open bug; the next rc's Bug window review judges the fixes
context: rc-9 shipped 0201/0204's 'the next rc's Job 1 resolves it' because the main thread's granularity-grill Q19 (2026-10-05) recommended reversing the operator's G2 ruling (2026-10-05T005326Z: a non-blocking bug's fix is pushed to the end of the same rc). The operator rejected the reversal on 2026-10-05.
decision: We will resolve every bug inside the rc that finds it; no rc ever closes with an open bug. A block-list bug (bugs law §2) is fixed at once as a hotfix. Any other bug is registered, found_in its rc, and resolved in that same rc by the bug batch: one job outside the DAG, after the DAG's last job merges and before the Reconciliation job, grouped by cause, a fix-induced one as a REBUILD; a bug found during Reconciliation is fixed inside it. The next rc's ## Bug window review judges those fixes (direction, what followed, KEEP or REBUILD) and its Job 1 executes the verdicts; it never inherits an open bug.
consequences: + An rc ships with zero open bugs and its fixes get a review one rc later. - The rc's DAG end waits on the bug batch; 0201's and 0204's next-Job-1 clauses are void.
measured_by: bugs.py status lists no open record found_in a closed rc; each rc SPEC's ## Bug window review table judges the previous rc's fixes

title: Every gate level reads its verify line from the work branch

The job level still read HEAD, so a task that broke the verify: line left a fix line pointing at the work branch that cleared nothing (review M1 of 18ccb7e1f), and a job could weaken its own verify: line.
decision: We will read the verify:, verify-stage: and verify-task: lines from the work branch's tracked AGENTS.md at every gate level; no worktree (task, stage or job) changes the command that judges it; a missing or unstartable line is fixed by the operator committing it on the work branch.
consequences: + One authority, one fix line that always clears its block; a job cannot weaken its own gate. - Changing a repo's verify line is an operator act on the work branch.
